# Johann August Starck,

->Doctor of Holy Scripture, Princely Hessian-Darmstadt Chief Court<-
->Chaplain, Consistorial Councilor and Definitor,<- <note>A "Definitor" was a high-ranking administrative official in the Lutheran church hierarchy of the time.</note>

->o n<-

# Crypto-Catholicism,

# Proselytizing,

## Jesuitism,
## Secret Societies

->a n d<-
->especially the<-

## Accusations

->made against him by the authors of the<-
->Berlin Monthly<- <note>The *Berliner Monatsschrift* was the premier journal of the Berlin Enlightenment, which frequently attacked Starck for his perceived mystical and pro-Catholic tendencies.</note>

->supported with<-
->Documentary Evidence.<- <insert>F. F.</insert>

---

# Part I.

---

> He was certainly right who first said that a good insult is always better received and remembered than a good argument. There is *the theory of journalism traced in two words.* <note>original French: "Celui la avoit bien raison, qui a dit le premier, qu'une bonne injure est toujours mieux reçue et retenue, qu'un bon raisonnement. Voilà la Theorie du Journalisme tracée en deux mots."</note>

->MERCIER, Scenes of Paris. Vol. IV. p. 254.<-

## Frankfurt and Leipzig,
## published by Johann Georg Fleischer, 1787.

<summary>This is the title page of Johann August Starck's 1787 polemic, in which he defends himself against charges of being a secret Catholic (Crypto-Catholic) and a Jesuit sympathizer. The work is a significant artifact of the late German Enlightenment's internal conflicts regarding religion and secret societies.</summary>

# Preface
## to the Public.

---

It is known throughout the world what the bookseller <term>Buchführer<gloss>A term for a publisher or bookseller during this period.</gloss></term> Mr. Friedrich Nicolai in Berlin and the two editors of the *Berlin Monthly* <note>The *Berliner Monatsschrift* was a key journal of the German Enlightenment, often critical of religious traditionalism.</note>—Mr. Dr. <note>The abbreviation 'D.' stands for Doctor.</note> F. R. Gedike and Mr. Dr. Biester—and their anonymous collaborators have for some years been telling the Protestant German public about a secret, abominable, and insidious conspiracy <term>Complott<gloss>A plot or conspiracy; in this context, it refers to the "Jesuit conspiracy" fears of the late 18th century.</gloss></term>. This plot, they claim, was devised by the Catholics for the destruction of Protestants, and several Protestants are said to have involved themselves in it in the most unscrupulous manner

If it were only a matter of my person, I would have remained silent despite all the intrusive demands. "I wrap myself in my virtue" <note>original Latin: "mea virtute me involuo," a quote from the Roman poet Horace meaning to find contentment and protection in one's own integrity regardless of external fortune.</note> is enough for me. Anyone who knows me personally must surely laugh at such accusations and charges; moreover, my most perfect **justification** <term>Justification<gloss>In this context, a "Rechtfertigung"—a formal defense or vindication of one's character, actions, and religious beliefs.</gloss></term> is found in my writings, which are in everyone's hands. Those who can still misjudge me after reading them deserve a shrug of the shoulders, but not a rebuttal. An upright and deserving man is not dishonored because an unknown or wicked hand throws mud at his coat. Neither, then, am I dishonored by those personal **slanders**. posted, so that if one of the two can be identified, they may be punished as they deserve; but the citizen mistreated in the <term>lampoon<gloss>original: Pasquill; an anonymous satirical or libelous writing posted in a public place to defame someone.</gloss></term> does not need to justify or defend himself before the public for that reason. My worldly fortune cannot be undermined by the slanders of my adversaries, so long as the **Princely House** <note>The author likely serves a specific German duke or prince, whose patronage provides social and financial security.</note>, which I have the good fortune to serve and which has granted me its grace and confidence, maintains the noble mindset that is natural to it and which it will not renounce. And what traveler is safe from being attacked and ruined in the middle of the highway by someone hiding in the bushes? But I know that God's hand is over us all.

According to these convictions of my heart, I should have said nothing, or only very little, to the public regarding all the attacks concerning my person. However, I am a **Protestant theologian**, and according to the oath I have sworn to my church, I am bound [to seek] its best interest...

--- Page 9 ---
<meta>This page continues the author's transition from a personal defense against libel to a professional defense of the Protestant church. He is responding to accusations leveled by the contributors to the Berlinische Monatsschrift, a prominent Enlightenment journal.</meta>

...to promote [its best interest], and to turn away all threatening harm to the best of my modest abilities. And according to this duty incumbent upon me, I have much—very much—to say. I must not only precisely and thoroughly refute the ugly accusations and charges that have been scattered against me; but also investigate and bring to light everything that the **Berlin Monthly writers** <note>The *Berliner Monatsschriftsteller* were contributors to the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, the premier journal of the German Enlightenment (Aufklärung), known for its rationalist critiques of religion.</note> have seen fit to spread throughout the world regarding the secret <term>machinations<gloss>original: Machinationen; schemes or underhanded plots.</gloss></term> of the **Catholics** intended for the ruin of our church. 

I must also examine, as thoroughly and exactly as I am able, the consequences to be expected from this, and the intentions they hope to achieve through this new **heresy hunt** <term><gloss>original: Ketzerjagd; a metaphorical "witch hunt" or aggressive persecution of those with differing religious views.</gloss></term>—which is so striking for our century <note>The 18th century, the "Age of Enlightenment," was seen by contemporaries as an era of tolerance; the author finds a "heresy hunt" particularly out of place in such a "civilized" time.</note>. In doing the former, I am doing nothing other than what those writers have so often, so urgently, so emphatically, indeed so boldly and shamelessly challenged me to do; and in doing the latter, I am doing what my office, calling, and duty—and I may add, the **welfare** of my Christian fellow-citizens and the honor of our century—demand of me.

<summary>The author asserts that his duty as a theologian compels him to refute personal slanders and investigate claims of Catholic conspiracies spread by Enlightenment journalists. He frames his response not as a personal vendetta, but as a defense of the Protestant church and the "honor" of the 18th century.</summary>
<keywords>Berlinische Monatsschrift, Catholic conspiracies, heresy hunt, Protestantism, Enlightenment, theological oath, religious polemics</keywords>

This was, as anyone must realize, an undertaking that has cost much time, effort, and patience. But a **peddler of anecdotes** <note>original: *Anekdotenkrämer*; a derogatory term for someone who deals in trivial stories or gossip rather than substance.</note> who also traveled—although he was not as famous a traveler as Mr. Nikolai <note>Friedrich Nicolai (1733–1811) was a leading figure of the Berlin Enlightenment, famous for his extensive travel writings and rationalist critiques.</note>—and who, as "thanks" for the kind hospitality enjoyed in my home, had all sorts of things—true, false, and distorted—about me inserted into Mr. <term>Court Councilor<gloss>Hofrath; a title given to high-ranking officials or distinguished scholars in German-speaking lands.</gloss></term> Meusel’s *Historical Literature* <note>Johann Georg Meusel (1743–1820) was a renowned bibliographer; his *Historische Literatur* was a major scholarly journal of the time.</note>, nonetheless said of me that I am very painstaking in my work.

That he spoke a grain of truth amidst so many falsehoods, I intend to prove through an investigation as painstaking as this one, and I will not knowingly overlook a single matter in the entire *Monthly* <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift*.</note> concerning <term>crypto-Catholicism<gloss>original: Krypto-Katholicismus; the secret practice of Catholicism while outwardly professing Protestantism.</gloss></term> and <term>Jesuitism<gloss>original: Jesuitismus; refers to the practices of the Jesuit Order, often used as a slur to imply secret plots or manipulative theology.</gloss></term> without examining it closely. The public will thus receive from me a completely impartial and as precise an investigation as has been possible for me.

<summary>The author defends his scholarly diligence against a former guest who published disparaging remarks about him, promising a thorough and impartial investigation into claims of secret Catholic influence.</summary>

But since I—after having carefully gone through everything that the **monthly writers** <note>Referring to the contributors of the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, a leading journal of the German Enlightenment.</note> have dangled before the public regarding this matter, including their reasons, so-called facts, and proofs (and I must confess that, although I felt innocent, I was actually so far deceived in the beginning as to believe there might indeed be something to this unbelievable matter)—must now declare the whole claim to be an adventurous **chimera** <note>A "chimera" refers to a wild, groundless illusion or a fabrication of the mind.</note>, I can certainly expect a terrible clamor. That does not concern me: for I am none of these things; and can one say worse things about me than what has already been said and believed—likely not by the healthy, but by the sick public? <meta>This page continues the author's critique of the manipulative tactics used by his intellectual opponents. It follows the previous page's mention of the "artifices" or clever tricks employed by certain writers to discredit their targets.</meta>

...pass over things as if they had never been said at all, but latch onto other matters instead, expounding upon them with much **declamation** <note>original: *Deklamation*; here referring to loud, rhetorical speech-making intended to sway emotions rather than offer logical proof.</note>, and shifting the point of view. This is exactly what was done against **Professor Garve** <note>Christian Garve (1742–1798), a popular philosopher of the German Enlightenment.</note>, **Lavater** <note>Johann Caspar Lavater (1741–1801), a Swiss poet and theologian famous for his work on physiognomy.</note>, and **Sailer** <note>Johann Michael Sailer (1751–1832), a Catholic theologian who sought to reconcile Enlightenment thought with Christian faith.</note> by **Mr. Nicolai** and **Mr. Biester** <note>Friedrich Nicolai and Johann Erich Biester were central figures of the Berlin Enlightenment and editors of the influential journal *Allgemeine Deutsche Bibliothek*; they were known for their fierce, often dogmatic, critiques of anything they deemed "obscurantist" or mystical.</note>.

Or they seat themselves upon their throne and pass judgment, or they decry what they cannot refute as **unfounded** <note>original: *ungründlich*; lacking depth or a solid basis.</note>, or label the author as "weak." This is how Mr. Nicolai dealt with the excellent letters of the worthy **Superintendent de Marees** <note>Adolph Ludwig de Marees (1734–1789), a high-ranking church official in Dessau known for his theological writings.</note> in **Dessau**, which certainly testify to much true and thorough **theological scholarship**. In this way, our German **public** <note>original: *Publikum*; the reading public or "Republic of Letters."</note> is deceived and led away from the main issues in the most artificial manner. They cast accusations before the public, frequently repeat them themselves, have them repeated by others, and then continue to build further upon them; thus the public is deceived once again, since the initial premise on which they founded the latter had not even been proven. They po- <note>The text cuts off mid-word (*stellen*); the catchword indicates the sentence likely continues with "pose" or "position."</note>

# On Crypto-Catholicism and Jesuitism #

In the Netherlands, it is said that the Jesuits and Catholics play a role: and generally, wherever one turns, that hated ghost stands before one's eyes, the *pestilence that stalks in the darkness* <note>original: "Negotium ambulans in tenebris"; a reference to Psalm 91:6, frequently used in this period to describe perceived secret threats or conspiracies.</note>, which threatens to swallow the Protestant Church. Everything, if one trusts the reports of these men, is dangerous and suspicious. Not only the so-called secret societies—such as the **Order of Freemasons**, which until now did not concern itself with religion at all; the **Order of the so-called Gold and Rosicrucians** <note>An esoteric brotherhood claiming to possess ancient secret wisdom; they were often accused of being a front for Catholic counter-revolutionary efforts.</note>; the **Order of Divine Providence**; the **Martinists** in France <note>Followers of Louis Claude de Saint-Martin, who focused on mystical Christianity and theodicy.</note>; and **Mesmer’s followers** <note>Adherents of Franz Mesmer, who practiced "animal magnetism," a precursor to hypnotism that many Enlightenment thinkers viewed as occultist nonsense.</note>; and whatever other varieties of these may exist—but even the **Society for the Preservation of Pure Doctrine and the Promotion of Godliness**, which unites for the maintenance of the **Lutheran religious concept** according to the **Augsburg Confession** <note>The primary confession of faith of the Lutheran Church and one of the most important documents of the Protestant Reformation.</note>; even the efforts to unite the three religious parties <note>The three main Christian denominations in the Holy Roman Empire: Lutheran, Reformed (Calvinist), and Catholic.</note> (which, although held by others to be impossible, undesirable, or even harmful, nevertheless—

<meta>catchword: from</meta>

---

—[from] a cloister at the Cathedral, and on the churchyard on the so-called "poor side," they were permitted to bury their dead, and in total silence. Whether they have been granted more freedoms since that time out of Christian tolerance; whether it was deemed necessary to allow them a school so that the small portion of Catholic subjects would not grow up without instruction, I do not know. That the wise and excellent ruler of my fatherland should permit a seminary, a "secret nest" for missions, or a nursery of **Jesuitism** in his land is incredible. It is the duty of the insightful ministers of this Prince to hold those to account who attach this stain to the Mecklenburg government and the land, which has always kept itself pure since the **Reformation**.

### Proselytizing and Secret Societies. 13 ###

I was forced to recognize immediately the unbelievable and contradictory nature of these claims, which allowed me to think as **Aemilius Paullus** <note>original: "Emil"; referring to Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus (c. 229–160 BCE), a Roman general and statesman.</note> did when he wrote to the Senate during the **Macedonian War**: *Do not nourish rumors with your credulity, for which no author will stand forth* <note>original Latin: "Vos rumores credulitate veſtra non alatis, quorum auctor nemo exſtabit."</note>. Consequently, I could remain quite silent and leave everything to God and to time. Yet this was more than mere literary teasing or journalist sniping; it was a personal, poisonous attack that destroyed honor and a good name—a formal <term>lampoon</term> <note>original: "Pasquill"; a published piece of writing that maliciously mocks or slanders a person.</note>. It was no longer the sort of thing that could be mediated through a scholarly feud, but rather something that had to be brought before the authorities for punishment and legal satisfaction.

And such a lampoon—which any man of honor and sensitivity would have rejected with indignation had it been sent to him—was posted against me in their monthly journal by two men who hold public offices of honor. One is a <term>Superior Consistorial Councilor</term> <note>original: "Oberconſiſtorialrath"; a high-ranking official in the administrative council of the Protestant church.</note> who sits in a council alongside men like **Teller, Spalding, Büsching, Silberschlag,** and **Dietrich**; the other is a Royal Librarian who, as a Doctor of Laws, must have been sufficiently aware of the infamy of <term>libelous writings</term> <note>original Latin: "libelli famosi"</note> and the penalties that await those who boldly and intentionally distribute them!

Despite all this, however, I was still not explicitly named. Even though various friends wrote to me saying that I was the intended target, and even though they finally made it so obvious that the public was bound to realize it, and I myself could conclude it from various passages of the attacks made against me—I was still not named. Had I wanted to come forward and defend myself then, opponents of this sort would always have applied the old proverb: *He who excuses himself, accuses himself!* <note>original French: "Qui s’excuſe, s’accuſe!"</note>

## On Crypto-Catholicism and Jesuitism, ##

...they made these claims against me—for what do these people *not* know how to assert! And in the end, they would have always had a loophole remaining: that they did not specifically mean me, and that I must simply be feeling my own guilt. Therefore, I had to wait in patience until they reached the full measure of their audacity and actually named me.

## On Alleged Crypto-Catholicism.
<term>Crypto-Catholicism; from the Greek "kryptos" (hidden), this refers to the secret practice of Catholicism while publicly professing to be Protestant. In this period, it was a common and serious accusation used to discredit public figures.</term>

These troubles were stirred up around the year 1570 by Peucer <note>Caspar Peucer (1525–1602), a scholar and physician who was a key figure in the "Philippist" movement following the death of his father-in-law, Melanchthon.</note>, Melanchthon's son-in-law, and various theologians at the two universities of Wittenberg and Leipzig. ...prolonged and difficult imprisonment, and finally the beheading of Chancellor Crell <note>Nikolaus Krell (c. 1550–1601) was the Chancellor of the Electorate of Saxony. However, as sad as this entire conflict was, both in the way it was conducted and in its effects and consequences, the opponents of the so-called Crypto-Calvinists <term>Crypto-Calvinism; a term used by "Gnesio-Lutherans" (strict Lutherans) to describe those suspected of secretly introducing Calvinist theology into the Lutheran Church, particularly regarding the nature of the Lord's Supper.</term> still deserve some measure of excuse. Those times were the era of vigorous polemic; philanthropic tolerance and Christian forbearance were virtues still very unknown among theologians, and which one could not easily practice without making oneself suspect. # Catholicism

<header>Catholicism</header>

...parts wish to see, [they know] far too well how much their ancestors gained through the Reformation in terms of territorial sovereignty, land, and income <note>The footnote below elaborates on the legal and financial gains of the Protestant estates.</note>, and how much the Protestant religion itself contributes to the culture of their lands and the prosperity of their subjects. Their episcopal rights <note>The rights of a bishop, which in Protestant territories were often assumed by the secular prince (Summepiskopat).</note> and everything belonging to the **rights concerning sacred matters** <term>original: *juribus circa sacra*; the legal authority of a sovereign over the external affairs of the church within their territory.</term> are far too precious to them to let all this be snatched away again. They would not favor Catholicism, allow monasticism and ignorance to spread among their subjects once more, or permit a nest of priests to settle in their midst again.

---

*) Anyone who is not already familiar, as a political scientist or historian, with the highly significant increase in power, prestige, sovereignty, and revenue that our Protestant imperial estates owe to the Reformation alone, can find detailed instruction in von Meiern’s *Acts of the Peace of Westphalia and its Execution at Nuremberg*. <note>Referencing the 1648 Peace of Westphalia, which codified the legal rights of Protestants in the Holy Roman Empire.</note> Compare also I. H. By defending freedom of conscience, it simultaneously led the Princes of Germany to more fully extract from antiquity and legitimate sources that eminent liberty which they enjoy as estates. Rather, it has served to make Protestant subjects keep a watchful eye on every step of their prince if he had adopted the Catholic religion, and to secure Protestantism. And the more the **Enlightenment** <term>original: *Aufklärung*; the 18th-century intellectual movement that emphasized reason, science, and individual rights over traditional dogma.</term> has increased among Protestants, the rarer the transitions to the Papacy have become. Our German princes also know, if they only look at their worldly advantages...

He is not omnipresent, to ensure the necessary obedience everywhere. And where is the state in which the regulations of the ruler are always and everywhere punctually fulfilled?

<header>On the Alleged Crypto-</header>

The most obvious objection that can be raised against my convictions—which are based on the entire state of Protestantism and Catholicism, and hold that the whole pretense of secret machinations by the Catholic Church for the ruin of Protestantism is groundless, and that nothing is to be feared from any such machinations should they even exist—is this: "We admit," they say, "that previous projects have failed. Polemical sermons, polemical writings, overt Papist missionaries, formal disputes, and methods of church union <note>Efforts to reconcile the Protestant and Catholic churches, which were often viewed with suspicion by hardline Enlightenment thinkers as "Trojan horses" for a Catholic takeover.</note> no longer achieve anything; but for that very reason, other means are now being employed that are not as worn out as those. Instead of the former overt missionaries, secret ones are now used, whose true nature cannot be seen. Secret societies are utilized for this purpose; they seek to win over the Protestants in secret, to give them back a taste for superstition, miracles, and stupidity, and to plunge them back into the old barbarism. Above all, the Jesuits are active in this—who, though externally suppressed <note>The Society of Jesus (Jesuits) was officially suppressed by Pope Clement XIV in 1773, but many members continued to work as secular priests or within other organizations, fueling conspiracy theories that they were operating in the shadows.</note>, nevertheless continue their institute and play their secret game in secret societies and among individual persons. The more secret and hidden all this is conducted, the more dangerous it is, and never has the danger been as great as it is right now. We are the upright men who discover these secret passages and tricks, sparing no effort, labor, time, or expense; we travel and correspond to bring everything to light. We keep watch while our Protestant teachers sleep, and we warn our contemporaries of the horrific danger hovering over their heads."

...must travel in order to hold Catholic worship services for the cavalry and infantry regiments stationed in garrison there, for which the necessary relay teams <note>original: *Vorspann*; the historical practice of requiring local citizens to provide fresh horses and wagons for official travelers</note> are provided to him \*). However, the location assigned to the Catholics for worship on these occasions was generally of such a nature that it was so highly inconvenient and undignified for that purpose, that if the specific details had been sufficiently known to the tolerant Prussian government, they certainly would have seen to a better arrangement themselves. This is especially true since foreign recruitment brought more and more Catholic recruits into the country, and through the paternal measures of the Monarch <note>Likely referring to Frederick the Great or Frederick William II, whose policies encouraged immigration to boost the population</note>, the mass of the people has increased unbelievably according to public accounts; thus, through new settlers, the small flocks of Catholics grew into full congregations. Yet, things were simply as they were.

Where the Catholics held their worship, the location in some towns was a local inn; and now this one, now that one was assigned for the purpose. Consequently, it often happened that the room intended for the service was occupied by traveling strangers; the clergyman had to spend the night in the innkeeper’s own living room, then wait with his congregation for the strangers to depart, and only then could he hold the service in the room just vacated by the travelers. In some towns, these rooms were very low-ceilinged and so cramped that they could hardly hold 50 to 60 people, and yet the congregation was over a hundred strong; many people therefore actually fainted. And yet, in this crush, confession had to be heard \*\*) and Communion held. Otherwise:

**Father Schorenstein** <note>original: *Pater Schorenstein*; a Catholic priest and apologist.</note> explains himself very elaborately regarding the accusation made by the **Acatholicus** <note>original: *Akatholikus*; Greek/Latin for "The Non-Catholic." He argues that **missionaries** <note>original: *Missionarien*</note> were not always sent out to make **proselytes** <note>original: *Proselyten*; new converts to a religion.</note>, but only to instruct those who could have no pastors in Protestant lands and to administer the **sacraments** <note>original: *Sacramente*</note> to them; and the actual main purpose of the missionaries was really to convert those to Christianity to whom it was still completely unknown *). As true as all of this may be in part, **Father Schorenstein** does not sufficiently refute the accusations of the **Acatholicus** here. To be unwilling to allow Catholics in Protestant lands to send their children to Catholic lands to have them educated there in the principles of their religion would indeed be **intolerance**, **coercion of conscience**, and the most blatant injustice. ## Further Steps of the Berlin Monthly Periodical Contributors

...Catholics and Protestants are litigated in court, where it is solely a matter of legal grounds and the observation of all legal formalities, and where the granting of religious services could be cited as proof of an interrupted statute of limitations <term>statute of limitations</term> <note>original: *Verjährung*; the legal principle where a right is lost if not exercised, or a claim is barred after a certain time. In this context, it refers to the fear that allowing Catholics to use a church would legally weaken the Protestants' sole claim to the property over time.</note> of possession against the Protestants.

Should the Catholics become masters again and think as they once did, it would be of no help to the Protestants that they had locked their churches ever so carefully during their possession: they would not allow the right of prescription <note>A legal term for acquiring a right through long-term use or possession.</note> to stand; rather, the previous lack of cooperation by the Protestants would make them even harsher in the exercise of their victory. But if the Pope and the clergy <note>original: *Klerisey*</note> did not regain their former dominion, it would also not harm the Protestants that they had, at most, given the Catholics a very slight appearance of a claim against them. 

The caution demonstrated by the refusal of the churches would therefore be far too little if the world were suddenly to lapse back into superstition and slavery, and far too much if it retains its Enlightenment <note>original: *Aufklärung*</note>. It is far more important that we seek to preserve our Protestant principles than that we entrench our churches; and these principles bring tolerance with them, regarding which Professor Garve expresses himself very beautifully. The assertion of these advantages, he says, must be worth more to us than securing the property of our churches against future legal chicanery. 

But this advantage, it is said in conclusion, the Catholics will not concede to us much longer, since even in my own fatherland there are cases where Catholic churches have been granted for the performance of Protestant religious acts.

## Secret Proselytizing, and the Means Allegedly Serving It.

The writers of the **Berlin Monthly** had already, in the February issue of 1784, given various hints about the secret intentions and schemes of the Catholics to ensnare and subjugate the Protestants. At that time, however, they were primarily concerned with the **granting of Protestant churches for Catholic worship**. In the following year, 1785, they move closer to the heart of the matter and gradually present the major facts intended to prove their allegations of secret deceptions by the Catholics and to justify their warnings regarding the great dangers facing Protestants. It is extraordinarily difficult to pave a path through this wild, overgrown thicket of thorns. Not just one or two writers are speaking, but several. Each throws his stone onto this general heap of rubble. <term>Ex-Jesuits<note>Former members of the Society of Jesus after the order was suppressed by the Pope in 1773; they were frequently accused of continuing their work in secret.</note></term>, secret societies, <term>Rosicrucians<note>A mystical secret society claiming ancient esoteric knowledge, which gained significant influence in the Prussian court of Frederick William II.</note></term>, <term>Illuminati<note>An Enlightenment secret society founded in Bavaria that sought to oppose religious influence in public life; they were often the targets of counter-conspiracy theories.</note></term>, religious unification, <term>Massius<note>Likely referring to a specific controversial figure or polemicist involved in the religious debates of the 1780s.</note></term>, Protestants who are allegedly secret Catholics, <term>Freemasonry<note>A fraternal organization that Enlightenment thinkers and their opponents both used as a vehicle for their respective ideologies.</note></term>, false tolerance, <term>Divine Order<note>original: "Ordre divin." This may refer to the work of Johann Peter Süssmilch on population statistics or a specific theological concept of the era.</note></term>, <term>Claudius<note>Likely Matthias Claudius, a popular poet and journalist who became increasingly critical of the rationalist Enlightenment.</note></term>, <term>Magnetismus<note>Referring to "Animal Magnetism" or Mesmerism, a popular medical and spiritual fad that many Enlightenment thinkers viewed as a gateway to superstition.</note></term>, <term>Cagliostro<note>Count Alessandro di Cagliostro, a famous occultist and self-proclaimed magician who epitomized the "irrational" side of the late 18th century.</note></term>,

One is undecided as to what to tackle first. This may be coincidental; but this Babylonian confusion is an almost insurmountable obstacle for anyone who wants to investigate the matter closely. One cannot pick up a single piece without grasping ten others; none exists entirely and solely on its own, but rather in every individual piece there are particles of the others. To judge one subject, one must read them all, and must do so again every time one intends to examine a different subject from what has already been read. So artfully is this work constructed, though it aims at a single purpose. The most patient reader must therefore grow weary of the investigation and is ultimately brought to believe that which is presented with the greatest probability; one gradually forgets the rules by which one must investigate. The frequent repetitions and declamations stun; the frequent assurances of integrity, love for the welfare of mankind, concern for religion, and whatever else they are called, eventually win one over. From a state of believing nothing, one moves unnoticed toward believing something, and finally to regarding everything as well-founded, and the **cunningly spread** <note>original: "Callide vulgata" — likely the start of the Latin maxim "Callide vulgata, temere credita" (cunningly spread, rashly believed).</note>, te—

But what could Mr. Nicolai have been thinking when he recounts the specific literary needs of the Catholic confession—an extensive Canon Law <note>original: "*Jus canonicum*." The body of laws and regulations made by ecclesiastical authority for the government of a Christian church.</note>, a specialized study of its history and antiquities, and a Catholic-theological philosophy—and wants to persuade us that this indeed very specialized literature for Catholic Germany is so little known in the Protestant world that many Protestants cannot even imagine such a thing still exists? Where is the Protestant theologian, who is not merely a preacher but a scholar, who does not know all of this? Where is the Protestant jurist in the academies, and in some cases even in the courts of law, who does not have to study, use, and often even issue judgments according to the Catholic Canon Law <note>original: "*Jus canonicum Catholicorum*."</note>? 

It is unbelievable that Mr. Nicolai, who wishes to be seen as so learned, should not know such a thing. All this nitpicking, then, is to be seen as nothing other than the first rallying cry of the "Watchman of Zion" <note>original: "Zionswächters." A term often used for a self-appointed defender of the faith; here it is used sarcastically to describe Nicolai’s alarmist warnings about a "Catholic threat."</note> to the Protestant public: "You people, do not be so careless! Get to know your sworn enemies, the Catholics, better! Tremble at the danger being prepared for you! Be alert and watch!!!!"

[...were these countries] Protestant, and had Protestant rulers whose conversion to the Catholic Church resulted in Protestantism being displaced again, and the formerly displaced Catholic religion becoming dominant once more? One would almost think that Mr. Biester had never read history. Even though significant Protestant communities had gathered in France, Austria, and Hungary—who owed their good fortune partly to indulgent governments and partly to other circumstances—Catholicism nevertheless always remained the dominant religion in these countries, while Protestantism, by contrast, was only tolerated with more or less freedom. The rulers were collectively Catholic, and not Protestants who, through their conversion to the papacy, then became persecutors of their former religion and could displace Protestantism. But when stronger rulers ascended the throne in these countries and no longer believed that political necessity required them to be indulgent toward Protestants, the rulers (who had always been Catholic) and the Catholic Church (which had always remained dominant) began to restrict and perhaps entirely suppress the Protestants who had previously been treated with more indulgence. 

In France, the Protestants owed their exceptionally great privileges or freedoms only to the weak governments under Francis II, Henry II, and Henry III <note>Francis II (r. 1559–1560), Henry II (r. 1547–1559), and Henry III (r. 1574–1589) were kings during the French Wars of Religion, a period of intense civil infighting between Catholics and Huguenots (Protestants).</note>, and they were always at odds <note>original: "in den Haaren liegen"; literally "to be in each other's hair," an idiom for constant quarreling or conflict.</note> with the dominant Church and the rulers devoted to it. They pursued a different path—one safer for them, but also more spiteful and, to anyone with a shred of decency, more loathsome. Whatever they had either devised in their own heads or hatched in their corrupted hearts—as was partially the case with Dr. **Urlsperger** and Mr. **Lavater**—or whatever was sent to them by Deacon **Seidel** at St. Sebald’s Church in Nuremberg <note>St. Sebaldus Church is one of the most important medieval churches in Nuremberg; at the time, it was a center of Lutheran orthodoxy.</note> for the **moral poisoning** <note>original: "moralischen Vergiftung"</note> of his colleague, Mr. **Dreykorn**, (or whoever else his accuser may have been), or by masked, malicious people, as happened in my own case and as they have done on several other occasions: they posted it publicly.

In this way, they sought to support their **chimera** <note>A "chimera" refers to a grotesque or foolish fancy; here, the author means a manufactured conspiracy theory.</note> of **Crypto-Catholicism** <note>The "Krypto-Katholicismus" scare was a common Enlightenment-era conspiracy theory suggesting that secret Jesuits were infiltrating the Protestant church to bring it back under the Pope's control.</note> and **proselytizing**—a theory actually devised to undermine Christianity itself. By doing so, they aimed to make men who are respected and loved in their own communities, and in some cases esteemed abroad, appear suspicious to the world and to their own fellow citizens. This is true **moral poisoning** <note>original: "Giftmischerey," literally "the mixing of poisons," a term used here for malicious defamation.</note>, and is thus far more dangerous and abominable than an open, legal attack before the authorities! 

Had the authorities in all these places not been more insightful and better-minded, what else would have arisen in every location but an **Inquisition**? Perhaps not a direct one, but certainly an indirect one. In an even more spiteful and guileful manner, the governments have been called upon by Mr. **Biester** and his associates; the reproach made against them in **Schlözer’s State Gazette** <note>The *Staatsanzeigen*, edited by August Ludwig von Schlözer, was one of the most influential political journals of the German Enlightenment, known for its criticisms of government abuse.</note> is, to the shame of our times, only too well-founded. An Inquisition, whether it be a Venetian State Inquisition or a Spanish Inquisition of Faith, remains always an Inquisition—and those who provoke it are...

-> **Secret Proselytizing**, <-

an outcast of humanity, which must rightfully make everyone shudder. And this miserable trade, which **J. Biester** <note>Johann Erich Biester (1749–1816) was a leading figure of the Berlin Enlightenment and editor of the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*. I think, however, that through these smooth words and hypocritical whitewashing of the ugliest trade that anyone can practice, no one will allow themselves to be led astray or blinded from seeing the matter in its true form. Such cover-ups and whitewashing can mislead no one: the card shark, after all, also calls his dishonorable trade *correcting fortune* <note>original: "corriger la fortune," a French euphemism for cheating at cards.</note>, the mistress calls her dissoluteness and excesses "gallantry," and the Arabian robber calls his highway robbery "profit bestowed by God." No vice wants to be called by its true name, but always by a milder one.

So it may also not please Mr. **Biester** that he and his associates were accused in **Schlözer's** *State Reports* <note>The *Staatsanzeigen* was a highly influential political periodical edited by August Ludwig von Schlözer, known for its critical stance on government and social issues.</note> of having called upon governments to act as a kind of **Chastity Commission** <note>The *Keuschheitskommission* was a morals police force established by Empress Maria Theresa in Vienna to combat prostitution and adultery; here, it is used as a metaphor for intrusive state surveillance of private beliefs.</note> against the abuses of secret societies. Certainly, he has made a great effort for himself to [support] the [charges] already given to him by others...

# Secret Proselytizing

...to argue that this work is directed by certain unknown superiors <note>A common trope in 18th-century conspiracy theories, suggesting that secret societies like the Freemasons were controlled by "Unknown Superiors" (*unbekannte Oberen*) with hidden, often Jesuitical, agendas.</note>, that the Freemasonic Order itself is being misused for this purpose, and that truly great strides toward this goal have already been made? The reader who only reads superficially, and whose task it is not to examine the whole matter precisely and thoroughly, will—upon reading such a declamation, one impudent assertion after another—finally be deceived, hoodwinked, and ultimately led to believe the entire chimera <note>In this context, a "chimera" refers to a wild, unfounded illusion or a fabrication of the mind.</note>. Every new repetition of it, as is the intent, is then viewed as a new confirmation.

This anonymous author also does nothing but repeat what the monthly journal writers <note>Referring to the editors and contributors of the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, the flagship publication of the Berlin Enlightenment.</note> say about secret proselytizing, its supposedly great progress, and the means allegedly employed for it. He assumes these things to be true and proven, and then—as one might expect from such people—begins hurling accusations of "brutes," "worthlessness," and "intrigue," while labeling others "enemies of sound reason and Enlightenment" and "villains."

Whether the books he cites can truly and rightly be regarded as the offspring of students and affiliates of the allegedly unknown superiors, and thus as contributing to the supposed secret proselytizing, will be revealed when I investigate this matter myself. Whether his instigators <note>Original: *Vorbeter*, literally "those who lead the prayer," used here sarcastically to mean the intellectual leaders who provided the talking points for the anonymous author.</note>—who first invented that chimera for their criminal intentions—have proven their claims of secret proselytizing, its progress, and its methods, will be clear to every impartial reader. Such a reader, unless deafened by the loud clamor of the <term>Pseudo-Protestant guardians of Zion: a polemical term used by the author to mock self-appointed, overly zealous defenders of the Protestant faith who claimed to protect the "fortress" of Zion from Catholic influence</term>, will not have lost their capacity for thought and judgment, as will be seen from this entire section—

...be able to judge, and what follows will further enable him to do so. I now come to the ninth essay in this piece, which also comes from an anonymous source and bears the title: **The Supposed Inclination of Protestants toward Catholicism** *). Since this inclination among Protestants can hardly arise on its own, given their overall situation, it must have been instilled in them from the outside by others. From this perspective alone, this essay belongs to the subject I am dealing with here—namely, secret proselytizing <note>The practice of attempting to convert people to another religion or belief system, often used pejoratively in this period to describe Jesuit or Catholic efforts to win back Protestants.</note>. But it belongs here even more because of other circumstances appearing within it. I shall follow the author step by step, and hopefully, the reader will also find here no small evidence of the wretched reasoning of these monthly journal writers, their dishonest path, and their unpardonable ignorance in the field into which they have so recklessly ventured. The author says right at the beginning: "Regarding the actual inclination toward Catholicism, so much is clear so far that 1) on one side, many Catholics—some in a very secret manner—are **proselyte hunters**." Here we encounter the monthly writers again in their old ways, presenting their dreams and unproven facts...

...either by themselves or by others (for who can vouch, in the case of anonymous essays, whether Mr. Biester and Gedike are not themselves the authors, praising themselves as if it were done by strangers, and urging themselves to continue, in order to perform a juggling act <note>original: *Gaukelspiel*; refers to a deceptive illusion or a magician's trick intended to mislead an audience</note> for the public, as if all this were happening from others?) they present unfounded facts as realities to throw sand in the eyes of the public. They do this so that the reader—who either cannot judge for himself or is modest enough to prefer the judgment of others over his own—is led to think: "There must be some truth to the matter; perhaps I just do not see it clearly; here is another person saying it is so!"

That Catholics in general are inclined to attempt to convince others of their religious opinions is subject to no doubt at all. We all know this and have known it for a long time, without needing the monthly journal writers for it. They share this trait with all religious parties. The Protestant is as little exempt from this as the Jew and the Muslim; indeed, even the Naturalist and the Deist want to convert others. To this end, the Deist writes his contestations of supernaturalism, his praises of the pure religion of reason <term>Vernunftreligion: A core Enlightenment concept of a moral religion based on human reason rather than divine revelation or scripture</term>, and whatever else he is able to put forward. Everyone considers their own opinions to be the best and wants—whether it stems from vanity or from a love of humanity—to win others over to their opinions as well. 

This cannot surprise the monthly journal writers. After all, they themselves want others to believe their chimera of crypto-Catholicism and proselytizing, and they even become angry if one does not wish to be converted to their fanaticism <note>original: *Schwärmerey*; a pejorative term often used by Enlightenment thinkers to describe irrational religious fervor, which the author here ironically turns back against the editors themselves</note>,

They are more so than the Jews, who admittedly hold an even higher opinion of their spiritual advantages than the Roman Christians, but who, under the deep pressure of living among Christians, dare not venture forth with it.

They are no more so than Naturalism <term>Naturalism: A philosophical viewpoint that everything arises from natural properties and causes, excluding supernatural explanations</term>. ### Secret Proselytizing

[...a spirit] prevails, which one can only encounter among the old Catholic controversial preachers. Whoever cannot be convinced of this need only look at the tragedy being performed before our eyes, where writers—who are not ashamed to profess themselves followers of pure **Deism** <term>Deism: A rationalistic religious philosophy that believes in a creator who does not intervene in the universe, often used by Enlightenment thinkers to bypass traditional Church dogma</term> when it suits their convenience—hide themselves just as easily in the robes of Protestant **Watchmen of Zion** <note>A mocking reference to the Berlin Enlightenment figures like Friedrich Nicolai, who claimed to be guarding Protestantism against "crypto-Catholics" while actually promoting secularism</note>, just as a Chinese Jesuit could don the clothing of a Mandarin <note>A reference to the Jesuit practice of "accommodation" in China, where missionaries adopted local dress and customs to gain influence, here used as a metaphor for hypocrisy</note>. They cast suspicion on anyone who opposes them, so that all tongues and hands are paralyzed from writing anything against them and their hypothesis. And even if they do not formally and publicly call upon the governments to act, they certainly persecute as severely as Spanish **Inquisitors** ever could; by casting suspicion upon honest people who displease them and their followers, they prepare inquisitions—the failure of which to occur is to be attributed not to them, but solely to the wisdom of the authorities.

— That **Catholics** are inclined to convert others, like all religious parties, and that they have always been more inclined to do so than many other religious parties, is an established truth, without our needing to learn it first from the monthly writers <note>Referring to the editors of the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*</note>. But then he has certainly announced nothing new to us, nothing that should particularly provoke the **Protestants** to take up arms <note>original: *in Harnisch jagen*; literally "to drive into armor," meaning to incite to anger or defense</note> or demand their special attention; nothing that should concern them now more than before, or because of the Catholics more than because of the **Deists** and **Natu-** <note>The word is cut off by the page break; likely "Naturalisten" or Naturalists</note>

### Secret Proselytizing,

too poor for them; if they only believed that it could serve their purposes, even if only slightly embellished <note>original: "ausstaffirt," meaning decorated or rigged out</note>, they took it up and repeated it to the public with an air of importance. # Secret Proselytizing

...anything further relevant. And now for the result. I admit that the Roman Church is more inclined than other Christian **religious parties** to make proselytes <note>A "proselyte" is a convert from one religion or opinion to another. In this context, it refers to the Catholic effort to bring Protestants back to the Roman fold.</note>; this is a truth that no one who knows the history and doctrines of this Church can deny. I admit that the proselytizers of this Church do not always care whether one joins it for good or bad reasons, out of conviction or ulterior motives, or in what manner the proselyte is converted. There is likewise no doubt about this, given the examples that history can provide. I admit that the inclination toward proselytizing has not yet been entirely lost even now among very many individual members of the Roman Church, and that this Church as a church, and the Pope as its head, remain as inclined to make proselytes as ever. This is perfectly consistent with the view of **Catholicism** as the only religion through which one can be saved <note>original: "alleinseligmachenden," referring to the Catholic dogma that salvation exists only within the institutional Church.</note> and with the principles of the **hierarchy**. We have known all of this for a long time, and did not first learn it from the writers of the *Berlin Monthly* <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift* (1783–1796) was a key journal of the German Enlightenment, known for its focus on reason and its criticism of religious fanaticism.</note> or from Mr. **Nicolai** <note>Friedrich Nicolai (1733–1811) was a famous Berlin writer and bookseller who was particularly obsessed with uncovering what he believed were "secret Jesuits" trying to undermine the Enlightenment.</note>.

--- But that is also all that can reasonably be admitted, and against which neither Protestants nor Catholics will have any grounded objection. Given the entire current religious, literary, and political situation of the **Protestants**, however, there is far less to fear from this inclination of the Roman Church and its individual members toward proselytizing than in former times. Whoever does not want to believe this should only take to heart the current literary condition and the religious mindset among Protestants, which is distancing itself more and more from superstition and ecclesiastical compulsion,

Even if their neat co-conspirator, the author of the *Heretics’ Almanac* <note>Original: *Keßeralmanach* (Ketzeralmanach), likely referring to the polemical writings of Friedrich Nicolai or his circle, who cataloged "heretical" or "Jesuitical" tendencies in others.</note>, had not directly laid out his Deism for us—and he at least goes about his work half-honestly, and does not put on the mask of a Protestant "Guardian of Zion" <note>Original: *Zionswächter*, a term for self-appointed defenders of religious orthodoxy, here used sarcastically for Enlightenment figures pretending to protect the Church while undermining it.</note> even as he portrays Christianity as mere Naturalism—they have nevertheless done so by setting forth their own confession of faith, which they themselves call "pure Deism." This they have thoroughly demonstrated. The second thing they have proven is the existence of the Father of All Lies. To want to deny him now, when he has such a large and respectable offspring capable of leading an honest German public astray with their web of untruths, would be folly and sacrilege.

Yet they have put forward so much else besides—concerning Jesuits, secret Catholics, and secret societies—and have in some cases even named the persons who allow themselves to be used for the propagation of Catholicism. You, too, German public, shall be informed of these things in turn; and I do not doubt that the entire *Mystery of Iniquity* <note>Original Latin: *Mysterium Iniquitatis*, a biblical term (2 Thessalonians 2:7) referring to a hidden, lawless power or conspiracy working against the divine order.</note> will soon lie clearly before your eyes in all its winding paths, and the blue mist <note>A German idiom for a deceptive smoke screen or a delusion intended to trick someone.</note> that your "Guardians of Zion" presented to you with such boldness will vanish of its own accord.

## Of Jesuits, their real and alleged machinations to the detriment of the Protestants.

**A**mong all the spiritual orders of the Roman Church, not a single one has proven itself so industrious since its founding in upholding and spreading Catholicism and suppressing the Protestants as the Jesuit Order, founded in the century of the Reformation. It has therefore been called the "right arm" and the "bodyguard of the Pope," and it is no wonder that the writers of the *Berlin Monthly* <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, a leading journal of the German Enlightenment (Aufklärung) often critical of religious influence.</note> and their followers take notice of this Order in their warnings about secret proselytizing <note>The act of attempting to convert people to another opinion or religion.</note> and the spread of Catholicism. To pass over it in silence would certainly be an unpardonable mistake. In all the disputes that our theologians had with the Catholics in previous centuries, their main opponents were always the Jesuits: opponents of such importance that they even gave a new turn to the scholarship that had previously been common among Protestants. For as much as the Protestants had been averse to <term>Scholastic philosophy</term> <note>A method of critical thought dominated by academic logic and the reconciliation of faith and reason, which earlier Reformers like Luther rejected as overly complicated and "Aristotelian."</note> since the time of Luther—himself a great adversary of Aristotle and the Scholastics—they nevertheless found themselves compelled, following the <term>Colloquy of Regensburg</term> <note>A religious debate held in 1601 between Catholic and Protestant theologians to seek common ground, which ultimately failed.</note> where they disputed with the Jesuits Gretser, Tanner, and Sager, to apply themselves to Scholastic philosophy in order to be able to contest their opponents with even greater success using the same weapons they used against the Protestants *). At most of the colloquies <note>Formal conferences or debates on religious doctrine.</note> were—

...to the detriment of the Protestants.

whom the Jesuits, as the most skilled masters of disputation, positioned against the Protestants. At the Colloquy <note>A formal theological conference or debate common during the Reformation era.</note> at Emmendingen in 1590, the help of the Jesuits was already employed *). At Regensburg in the year 1601, the Jesuits Gretser and Tanner were the foremost disputants; in 1608 at the Colloquy at Schwalbach, the two Jesuits Becanus and Serarius paraded their skills; at the Colloquy at Samelschenburg in 1614, the Jesuit Augustin von Hildesheim was the most prominent disputant. At the Colloquy at Neuburg in 1615, the Jesuit Keller disputed against Doctor Heilbrunner from Tübingen, and so on several other occasions. 

Various Protestants who, in former times, converted to the Roman Church were persuaded to do so by the Jesuits. It was the three Jesuits Macedo, Molines, and Cassati who primarily brought about the change of religion of Queen Christina of Sweden <note>The daughter of the champion of Protestantism, Gustavus Adolphus; her conversion in 1654 shocked Europe.</note>. Landgrave Ernst of Hesse-Cassel, who entered the Catholic Church in 1648, was primarily moved to do so by Jesuits. Likewise, Duke Wolfgang Wilhelm of Palatinate-Neuburg was brought by the Jesuit Jakob Reihing to accept the Catholic religion, and so were several others. Thus, in addition to the public opponents of the Protestant Church and those who advised the use of the harshest means for the extermination of alleged heretics **), they have had various members among them who sought to lead the Protestants back to the Roman Church in a gentler manner.

# Of Jesuits and their Machinations #

...everywhere. Even if one assumes that everything which our new Guardians of Zion <note>original: "Zionswächter"; a mocking or polemical term used here to describe self-appointed defenders of Protestantism who were often prone to alarmism.</note> have said regarding the still-surviving Order of the Jesuits, the connections that the ex-Jesuits are said to still maintain among themselves, and their mania for making proselytes <term>Proselytes: New converts, specifically those being recruited from Protestantism into Catholicism.</term>, were as well-founded as they themselves could wish; nevertheless, this entire report is of such a nature that every unbiased person must necessarily doubt either the honesty or the factual knowledge of its author. He says, on the one hand, far too much, and on the other hand, far too little. Had he only said in general that even now the Jesuits have not ceased their old habit of proselytizing, one might perhaps have been somewhat grateful to him. But now he says too much by saying that one encounters them everywhere. 

The most harmful mistrust, extremely detrimental to civic peace and society, is spread by this malicious report. No one is anymore certain whether he is not embracing a Jesuit in his most proven and long-known friend; indeed, no Christian congregation is safe, wondering if their preacher and schoolteacher might not be a secret Jesuit, etc. If the author of this essay were not already known to us from the preceding section as a person of the most malicious intentions, one might clear him of the charge that he intended to sow distrust in Christian society <note>original: "Societät"; referring to the collective body of Christian believers and their social structures.</note> with this anecdote. But since we already know him—from the expressions examined in the previous section and found on page 63 of the *Monthly Journal* <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, the leading journal of the Berlin Enlightenment, edited by Gedike and Biester, which frequently published anti-Catholic warnings.</note>—as a partisan of the freethinking conspiracy <term>Freethinking conspiracy: A term used by conservative or religious writers to describe a perceived plot by Enlightenment "freethinkers" to undermine traditional religion and social order.</term>, his malicious intent is clear: that with his claim that one encounters—

# to the detriment of the Protestants. #

...one encounters Jesuits everywhere, etc., he has sought to sow suspicion and mistrust among the Protestants. But on the other hand, he also says far too little: for "everywhere" is far too broad an address. Let someone look for what is supposed to exist everywhere, and yet is seen by no one! If the author had intended to truly warn his contemporaries, he would have had to present them with better and more precise information. His report is undeniably intended to be a major fact, meant to show us all the horrors of Crypto-Catholicism <term>Crypto-Catholicism: The secret practice of Catholic faith while publicly professing to be Protestant, a major fear during the Enlightenment.</term> and secret proselytizing <term>Proselytizing: The act of attempting to convert people to another opinion or religion, in this case, from Protestantism to Catholicism.</term>. But to judge facts, as the monthly writers <note>original: "Monatsschriftsteller"; the authors contributing to the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, a leading journal of the German Enlightenment.</note> themselves say, they must be presented precisely and with all the circumstances; here, however, a true game of blind man’s buff <note>original: "Blindekuhespiel"; a metaphor for being led around blindly or deceived.</note> is being played with the public in an impudent manner. —

## Of Jesuits and their Machinations

The outward appearance of this, their new devil, they describe with the very same attributes with which the old devil was outfitted when old women or fearful children imagined him in material form—except that they have not yet scouted out the dragon’s tail, the goat’s horns, and the cloven hoof. In contrast, however, the inner nature of their new devil—his striving and his deeds—is all the more terrible, fearsome, and abominable. For example, the poor old devil was still said to occasionally find pleasure in a witty mind that he had made his own; but the new, barbaric devil makes people stupid, nails up their brains <note>original: "vernagelt ihnen das Gehirn". When the old devil possessed a person, he could not prevent his presence from soon being discovered; but the new one is of such a subtle, volatile nature that many a man might not even know that he is held in its claws. This goes so far that even the writers of monthly journals <note>original: "Monatsschriftsteller". These were the influential journalists and critics of the Enlightenment who published regular periodicals and shaped public opinion.</note> are not safe from being led on his leash, or from being a wire-puppet <note>original: "Dratpuppe". In this very same piece, in which Mr. Biester has shown himself from so many "splendid" sides <note>The author is being sarcastic here, mocking Biester’s perceived self-importance.</note>, he also comes to the Jesuits when speaking of the missionaries and the institutions established for the conversion of Protestants. # On Jesuits and their Machinations

...cius, who died in 1597, [in whose] funeral oration for Gregory XIII mention occurs of the various institutions established for the conversion of Protestants. One must truly be astonished at how a man can be so brazen as to refer to things that happened nearly 200 years ago in order to derive something for our own times; and perhaps Mr. Biester thinks he is thereby proving the industriousness of the Jesuits 200 years ago; yet even in this there is something flawed. For from the fact that Tuccius, who gave the funeral sermon, was a Jesuit, it does not follow that all conversion institutions established by Gregory XIII were Jesuit missions; and what does all this prove for the present times, which are so changed in every respect? 

But Mr. Biester does not speak merely of the zeal of the Jesuits and their conversion institutions 200 years ago; he artfully drags all this over into our own times, and says—regarding the words of Tuccius, *Dillinganum Germanis* <note>Latin: "The Dillingen [seminary] for the Germans."</note>—in a parenthesis: at Dillingen, the residence of the Bishop of Augsburg and a Catholic university, such a seminary has thus been established for us all. I find it hard to believe that one could carry this charade <term>charade: The original German "Gauckelspiel" refers to a juggling act, a deceptive trick, or a piece of stage-magic intended to delude an audience.</term> with the public any further than it is being carried here.

## On Jesuits and their Machinations

The author <note>Completing the word "Verfasser" from the previous page.</note> of this missive says it should be called *Roman Catholics* <note>original: "Catholiques Romains"</note>, although it must occur to everyone—as Mr. Biester <note>Johann Erich Biester (1749–1816) was a prominent Berlin Enlightenment figure known for his obsession with uncovering "secret Jesuits" hidden within Protestant society.</note> had said—that in the process of deciphering, not even a single stroke should be in vain. Yet here, one finds not only such a vain stroke between the C and the H, but even the H is so separated from the C and R by strokes that it must necessarily constitute a word of its own, and cannot well express the small *h* in the word *Catholique*. — Regarding the *Impartial Examination* <note>original: "Examen impartial"</note> as the key! — In this, too, dear reader, you will find nothing better—if you read through all seventy-two paragraphs, from the beginning, where it says: *I seek the Truth* <note>original: "Je cherche la Verité"</note>, to the end, where Mother *Eve* appears and closes with the words: *A good conscience is worth as much as great knowledge* <note>original: "Une bonne Conscience vaut bien la haute science"</note>—than the same kind of arbitrary whims that you have already read.

Were this *Impartial Examination* truly the work of a member of that society from which those mystical French books originate, and which they had lost, then indeed their own interpretation of their unintelligible language would be of great importance. But as can be clearly seen, it is the work of a stranger who was infected by the whim of **Crypto-Catholicism** and **Jesuitism**, and who now believes he sees his phantom everywhere, arbitrarily interpreting those incomprehensible books according to this whim. Tomorrow, a similar fanatic could appear and dream of **Crypto-Judaism**, and it would perhaps be even easier for him to encounter all of **Judaism** and all the absurdities of the **Talmud** and the **Kabbalistic philosophy** of the Jews within them. I cannot, however, withhold a serious observation from the public, and that is the harmful and dangerous element inherent in these arbitrary interpretations. If this were approved and became common practice in the world—and how easily folly spreads!—what would then remain secure? The most straightforward writer, should he have the misfortune of displeasing these literary despots, is in danger of having his writings "interpreted" and a meaning forced into his words that makes him most maliciously suspicious to his contemporaries. Every person of feeling must abhor such mischief just as much as they must vigorously work against it.

### On the Jesuits and their Machinations

(as they know best) <note>This continues a sentence from the previous page, likely referring to the education of the Illuminati's founders.</note> attended school with the Jesuits in his youth. For if all those who formerly learned reading, writing, Latin, and rhetoric from the Jesuits were to be considered Jesuits themselves, how numerous the Jesuits would be! But the author is actually speaking of the **Illuminati system** and its adherents in general, and these are now supposed to be Jesuits without even knowing it. 

According to this claim, the Jesuits must have either secretly crept in among the Illuminati, or influenced their founders to achieve hidden objectives through the **Order of the Illuminati**, so that all the Illuminati—even without knowing it—are Jesuits. That would certainly be very ingenious. 

But how does this agree with what this same author said previously: that the Jesuits had united with the **followers of Zoroaster** <note>A common 18th-century reference to the Gold and Rosicrucians, a mystical order often seen as the conservative, anti-Enlightenment rivals of the Illuminati.</note> in order to displace the Illuminati? Are they then working against themselves, against a system originating from them, against their own tools, and against the very plans to be carried out through them? 

**If a kingdom is divided against itself, how can it stand?** <note>A reference to Mark 3:24. The author is using biblical logic to point out the absurdity of the conspiracy theory.</note> 

The Illuminati are supposed to seek the advancement of the **Enlightenment** <note>The intellectual movement emphasizing reason and individualism over tradition.</note> in **Bavaria**, while the Jesuits try to prevent Enlightenment and strive to maintain ignorance and **priestcraft** <note>original: "Pfaffrey," a derogatory term used by Enlightenment thinkers to describe the perceived corruption and manipulative power of the Catholic clergy.</note>; and yet, the Illuminati are supposedly Jesuits without knowing it! This would mean the proponents of Enlightenment are the tools of those who promote ignorance, and that the Jesuits are driving out their own tools—acting, as it were, like one devil driving out another, as it is written in the **Gospel** <note>original: "Evangelio." A reference to Matthew 12:24-27, where Jesus responds to the accusation that he drives out demons by the power of Beelzebub.</note>. If these are not contradictions, then none exist anymore. Perhaps then we will finally be broken of that philosophical prejudice which suggests that a thing cannot both be and not be at the same time!

# On Jesuits and their Machinations

...an entire army of Jesuits has been discovered, appearing to be on the march to devour us. In the first place, Mr. Biester says that it is well known that the Jesuits claim their <term>dissolution</term> <note>The 1773 suppression of the Society of Jesus by Pope Clement XIV, which officially disbanded the order in most of Europe.</note> is legally null and void because it did not occur in a lawful manner through a decree of a Council, and they base their hope on seeing the act of dissolution one day annulled \*. Here I must pause: for in these few words already are found unproven assertions and contradictions with Mr. Biester’s own principles. That all Jesuits—both the ex-Jesuits found in Germany and those continuing in <term>White Russia</term> <note>The region of White Ruthenia (modern-day Belarus). Empress Catherine the Great of Russia refused to promulgate the Pope's decree, allowing the Jesuit order to survive there when it was banned elsewhere.</note>—supposedly hold their decree of dissolution to be null because it does not rest on a Council decree, is something Mr. Biester has proven with nothing at all; and by using the expression *well known* <note>original: "bekanntlich"</note>, he merely wishes to evade the proof that should be demanded. No Catholic can assert this, as the Jesuit Order is certainly not the only one that the Popes alone, without the involvement of a Council, have dissolved. Furthermore, the Jesuits continuing in White Russia do not appeal to the idea that they wish to continue lawfully because they were dissolved unlawfully, and thus the act of dissolution is null; rather, they use the pretext that the decree of dissolution was not <term>served</term> <note>The original term "insinuiret" refers to the formal legal delivery of a decree, without which it was argued the law did not yet take effect.</note> to them, but to the bishops, and that decrees of the Pope cannot have force where the <term>Sovereign</term> <note>original: "Regent"</note> does not wish them to have force \*\*. ### ...to the detriment of the Protestants.

...understood as mere metaphysics. — Could it really be that **Garve** has heard nothing at all of **Father la Chaise**? <note>François de la Chaise (1624–1709) was the Jesuit confessor to King Louis XIV of France, known for his significant political influence.</note> Could it be that the **Jesuit Peter** <note>Edward Petre (1631–1699), a Jesuit advisor to King James II of England; his influence was widely blamed for the king's downfall.</note>, who caused so much mischief in England and was more a foolish zealot than a cunning statesman, was truly unknown to him? Could **Father Wolf** <note>A Jesuit diplomat who assisted in the negotiations between the Elector of Brandenburg and the Pope regarding the Elector's elevation to King in Prussia in 1701.</note> be unknown to him, as a learned Prussian subject, who played such a role in the elevation of the **House of Brandenburg** to royal dignity?

But now you say, **Mr. Nikolai**, in order to truly humble **Mr. Garve**—and a man deserves as much, who imagines he can oppose the great **Nikolai**—that **Mr. Garve** shows great ignorance if he imagines that the Jesuit superiors never made use of magic, spirit-seeing, and the desire for secret arts to rule over regents. # 464 On Jesuits and Their Machinations
464

What, then, do all these citations by Mr. Nicolai prove to show that the Jesuits were Magi <note>practitioners of "high" magic or hidden arts</note>, visionaries, and the like? Nothing, absolutely nothing. That these people—Dee <note>John Dee (1527–1608), the English mathematician and occultist</note>, Kelly <note>Edward Kelley (1555–1597), an alchemist and medium who worked with Dee</note>, Meyer <note>likely Michael Maier (1568–1622), a famous physician and alchemist</note>, and Typotius—were directed by Jesuits has not been proven at all by Mr. Nicolai; and indeed, no one else says so either. He must have particularly secret reports about this, known only to him, which he is still keeping hidden <note>original: "hinterm Berge hält" — an idiom meaning to withhold information or keep a secret</note>. Now, if Mr. Nicolai did not know that these people were not Jesuits, then he is far more ignorant than Mr. Garve <note>Christian Garve (1742–1798), a prominent Enlightenment philosopher whom Nicolai frequently attacked</note>; he, who so impudently accuses Mr. Garve of ignorance, and meanwhile boasts so conceitedly of himself, claiming that he has studied the history of the Jesuits—which certainly seems to have been detrimental to his own mind—more closely than anyone! But if he did know this, and nevertheless cited these people as examples of Jesuit magic, and that—

Nikolai, in the additions printed before the 3rd volume <unclear>in</unclear> the 2nd volume, p. 53, did not yet dare to call Typotius a Jesuit, but only said one could suspect from his book that he was a secret Jesuit. Here, however, he is already bolder and positively calls him a Jesuit in secular clothing. In such gradations, writers who wish to force their thesis upon the world draw from their own imagination: first suspicion, and then certainty, until in the end they even believe themselves that the child of their imagination is the truth. I add one more thing: that neither Bayle <note>Pierre Bayle (1647–1706), author of the influential *Historical and Critical Dictionary*</note> (Vol. II, p. 386), nor Moreri <note>Louis Moréri (1643–1680), a French priest and encyclopedist</note> (Vol. IV, p. 516), nor Hoffmann in the *Universal Lexicon* <note>original: "Lexico univ."; referring to Johann Jacob Hofmann’s 1698 encyclopedia</note> (Vol. IV, p. 550) says the slightest thing about Typotius’s alleged Jesuitism. From their data <note>original: "Datis"</note>, one can rather conclude the opposite. From where, then, might Mr. Nikolai have his information? Yet, with visionaries, one must not ask: How do you know that?

->### to the detriment of the Protestants.<-

...with what has he authentically proven the still ongoing, restless activity of the Jesuits against the Protestants? With nothing! Except that he imagines seeing Jesuits everywhere. And even suppose he had proven it ever so much, why [the anger against the journal *Religionsbegebenheiten*]? Because incense of admiration was not scattered upon the visions of Mr. *Nicolai* and his associates regarding Catholicism, Jesuitism, and so forth. The book still had its good sale, even if Mr. *Nicolai* did not have a safe-conduct <term>Freypaß: literally a "passport" or "safe-conduct," here used metaphorically to mean a favorable review that allows a book to pass unchallenged into the hands of the public</term> written for it in his "library" <note>The "library" refers to Nicolai's journal, the *Allgemeine deutsche Bibliothek* (General German Library), which was the most influential review organ of the German Enlightenment.</note>. However, after it so happened that in the ninth volume, page 839 and following, a defense of the Superintendent and Professor *Schulz* of Giessen <note>Johann Heinrich Schulz (1739–1823), a theologian known for his radical Enlightenment views, often called "Pigtail Schulz" (*Zopf-Schulz*) because of his rejection of traditional clerical dress.</note> was inserted against the attack found in the *Nicolai* appendix to the seventh volume; then the literary despot flared up in righteous anger and decreed in his tribunal: for this, the editor (Professor *Köster*) shall be thrashed at the first good opportunity. The *Religionsbegebenheiten* <note>The full title was *Religionsbegebenheiten in Teutschland* (Religious Events in Germany), an influential journal edited by Köster that reported on contemporary church history and controversies.</note> meanwhile remained unchallenged, and nothing was said anywhere against the *Schulzian* defense. Only on the occasion that in the *Allg. deutsch. Biblioth.* Vol. 71, Part 2, the *Mainz Monthly*—in which, among other things, *Köster's* "Ethics" appears—was extensively reviewed, did Mr. *Nicolai* have the following printed on page 553:

> “*Köster’s* philosophical ethics is much praised; that was only fair: for this very weak man flatters the Catholics and especially the **Mainz theologians** again in a very crawling manner.”

Whoever reads this would believe that Mr. *Köster* had flattered the Catholics and Mainz theologians within a work of philosophical ethics. For it is difficult to persuade oneself that in a "library" which wishes to stand in the reputation of impartiality and infallibility, a favorable review found in *another* journal should be refuted merely by the despotic decree that the author is a "weak man" who flatters the Catholics in a "crawling way," without even indicating what that weakness consists of, or where and in what manner the [Catholics were flattered].

## To the disadvantage of the Protestants.

...formation <note>Completing the word "Reformation" from the previous page; here referring to the internal reforms of the Catholic Church.</note>, or as the monthly writers say, merely bait and a deceptive word: Is it the work of the Jesuits, who have pursued it?
