He was caught in the crossfire of contemporary debates over whether his teaching methods were influenced by Jesuit pedagogical traditions.</note> was brought to this favorable but incorrect judgment of the Jesuits by them, and led, as it were, by a string without knowing it? How long have people held favorable notions of the schools and instruction of the Jesuits without one being able to say that those who held this prejudice fell into the hands of the Jesuits! And granted, even if the Jesuits had artificially instilled these favorable notions of their schools in Mr. **Heinike**, and everything that Mr. **Nicolai** knows to provide as motivations for this were truly as he says, and what he says about them—why they did not introduce the **Rochow** method—were also true; can one therefore say of Mr. **Heinike** that he has fallen into Jesuit hands, and cite all this as a strange way in which one can fall into Jesuit hands where one least expects it? What wretchedness!

From **Steiner's** assertion, which Mr. **Nicolai** mentions on page 65, I have already spoken before. Given their continued existence in **Russia**, it can hardly be said that not a hair of them remains. <note>Following the papal suppression of the Jesuits in 1773, the order survived in the Russian Empire because Catherine the Great refused to recognize the decree, allowing them to continue their educational work.</note> But whether the German ex-Jesuits are also systematically connected with them, forming one body with them, and so forth—that is the matter for which Professor **Garve** <note>Christian Garve (1742–1798), an influential Enlightenment philosopher and translator of Cicero and Adam Smith.</note> rightly demands proof before one can lend credence to Mr. **Nicolai’s** assertions.

Finally, Brener says that **Eckart** <note>Anselm Eckart, a Jesuit missionary who had been imprisoned by Pombal for many years.</note> had sent him the **petition** <note>Original: "Supplik," a formal humble request or prayer for legal redress.</note> that had been handed to the King and Queen regarding thirteen questions that were to be put to Pombal, and the decree of the Queen that the **sentence against the Jesuits from 1759** should be investigated anew; all of this, he (Brener) had handed over to a French writer in order to have it inserted into the newspapers.

Where in this entire letter is there any trace of connections among the members of the Order, as there was before? But at the end stands something important: "the Assistant has judged." At this point, Mr. Nicolai makes the observation that one can see that the hierarchy of the Jesuits is still in operation. Which Assistant judged? Surely one who is or was an Assistant, such as Karea and Lubowicki, who are listed as Assistants in the reports on the Jesuits in White Russia <note>original: "Weiß-Reußen." This refers to modern-day Belarus. Now I should like to know how else one could name these men, other than "Assistants"? It proves the ongoing hierarchy in White Russia, but not for the entire Order. — Certainly, one does not know whether to wonder more at Mr. Nicolai’s insolence regarding this letter and his conduct concerning it, or at the incomprehensible gullibility of a portion of the public, which could let itself be dragged around by the nose <note>The German idiom "am Seil herumschleppen" (to drag around on a rope) implies being easily led or deceived.</note> so shamefully by such a man!

Traces of this are found everywhere. Anyone who does not understand enough Latin to understand the letter that Mr. Nicolai has brought forward as such an important document, or who is lazy enough not to look for themselves, or good-hearted enough...

# On the Jesuits and their Machinations

...that **Garve** <note>Christian Garve (1742–1798) was a prominent Enlightenment philosopher known for his "popular philosophy" and common-sense approach.</note> drives away the "itch for proof" \*)—they will surely prove it. With blind partiality, he seeks to forge weapons <note>original: *Bolzen zu drehen*, literally "to turn bolts." With the highest degree of intolerance, he endeavors to make the **Catholics** and the **Catholic religion** look ridiculous at every opportunity with the bitterest sarcasms. He demands that the **Catholic Church**—now, in these first years, even at the very dawn of the **Enlightenment**—should immediately abandon the very dogmas that distinguish them from us. 

His fiery zeal knows no patience and no waiting; he wants everything changed at once. Because he has not found this to be the case, he—along with his fellow "Zion-watchers," <note>original: *Zionswächter*. It is well known that whenever something finds its way to our insightful, enlightened, and reading public, and can constitute a profitable publishing item for the bookseller, a multitude of parrots and copyists then appears, wanting to earn something as well. One cannot expect, therefore, that I should go through and refute every scribble of our prolific writers concerning the Nicolai-Biester Jesuit question <note>Friedrich Nicolai and Johann Erich Biester were prominent figures of the Berlin Enlightenment who led a literary campaign against what they perceived as secret Jesuit influence in Protestant lands.</note> in succession, since my book must already exceed the limits I had originally set for it.

There is nothing to say about this, and the entire booklet contains nothing that one should not already find everywhere.

# On Jesuits and Their Machinations

[Regarding the matter] at hand, it is also found in Mr. **Nicolai’s** appendix, and has already been examined by me in the preceding pages. Mr. **Nicolai** and this author of the preface agree so precisely, as one can see, that one must have had the other’s manuscript before his eyes; and Mr. **Nicolai**, who wrote his appendix in 1786, must either have copied from this book published in 1785, or he and the author of the preface must be one and the same person. This is how these gentlemen operate: what one has said is cited again as a "significant new testimony" in order to gain credit for their follies and wicked plans—as if an unproven point became proven, and a falsehood became truth, simply because it is asserted by several people. ### ...to the detriment of Protestants.

# Religious Unification as a Means

...[pro]selytizing for that party to which they were most attached, has become mixed in. The same thing happened among the Christians; their teachers, who thought differently according to their various modes of representation <term>Vorstellungsarten</term> <note>The internal mental frameworks and cultural lenses through which an individual interprets concepts.</note>, robbed Christianity of its universality early enough. The separatist, who is strongly opposed to all sects, becomes a proselytizer for his own favorite opinions. The Deist <note>An Enlightenment-era thinker who believed in a creator based on reason but rejected miracles and divine revelation.</note> and the Naturalist, the most zealous religious unifiers that could possibly exist—who wish to bring all people to a universal religion of reason, providence, and the "All-Father"—are at the same time no less proselytizers than others. They demand not only the acceptance of certain main and fundamental doctrines but also the simultaneous rejection of all other convictions, which they call supernaturalism <term>Supernaturalismus</term> <note>The belief in divine revelation and events that transcend natural laws, which Enlightenment rationalists often criticized.</note>.

In this regard, the Roman Church stands in exact parallel with Judaism. # Religious Unification as a Means

It was said of **Masius’s** project for religious union: the author is sick in the soul; he should be bought a place in a hospital. — And now, **Catholicism** is scented everywhere. And if one asks for proof, everything is reduced to **Mr. Nicolai’s** and the ***Monatsschrift’s*** <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, a leading journal of the German Enlightenment, which often published polemics against perceived religious "obscurantism" or secret Jesuit influence.</note> equally baseless assertions, visions, and chimeras. In the May issue of the ***Monatsschrift***, the author gifts the public various anecdotes that have been brought to him from **Danzig**, **Pomerania**, etc., regarding the spread of **Catholicism**; and among these are also found two unexpected testimonies, which I have already dealt with in detail. In the first of these alleged unexpected testimonies, which stems from an Apocalypticist <note>A person who interprets contemporary events through the lens of biblical prophecy regarding the end of the world.</note>, the religious union is also mentioned, and it is cited from the opinion of **Mr. Crusius** <note>Christian August Crusius (1715–1775), a prominent philosopher and theologian who opposed the pure rationalism of the Enlightenment.</note> regarding the **Schröpferian** spirit-summonings, that **Schröpfer** had held seductive speeches about a religious union before reliable informants. # A.

## Most Serene, Most Puissant King,
## Most Gracious King and Lord!

Your Royal Majesty’s praiseworthy <term>love of justice</term> <note>original: "Gerechtigkeitsliebe," a standard rhetorical appeal to a monarch’s duty as the ultimate judge.</note> is so world-renowned that even the most humble stranger may take refuge in it with joyful confidence, and may expect protection and satisfaction if he is innocently persecuted by Your Royal Majesty’s subjects—if his honor and good name are stolen from him, and if, once he no longer possesses this "jewel," he is then to be completely suppressed. I am now placed in this situation, so tragic for me, in which nothing remains but to throw myself before the throne of Your Royal Majesty and, with the feelings of an innocent man whose honor and good name have been wounded in the most abominable way, to most submissively pray that justice might speak loudly from that throne for the persecuted stranger against the persecuting subject.

It is common knowledge what has been said for more than a year in the *Berlin Monthly* <note>original: "Berliner Monatsschrift," a prominent journal of the Enlightenment edited by Friedrich Gedike and Johann Erich Biester</note>, regarding the secret machinations of the Catholics and <term>Jesuits</term> <note>The Society of Jesus had been suppressed by the Pope in 1773, but many continued to work in education or were suspected of working in secret, a common anxiety among Enlightenment thinkers.</note> to the detriment of Protestantism. I shall leave it undecided whether those secret efforts are well-founded, and if they were well-founded, whether they could ever be carried out; whether the violence of expression with which they are written about in the aforementioned monthly journal is consistent with the <term>tolerance</term> <note>A reference to the religious tolerance policies championed by the Prussian monarchy.</note> that first gained its existence under Your Royal Majesty’s most praiseworthy reign and now seems to be spreading beneficially throughout all of Germany; and whether that violence does not once again kindle mistrust, suspicion, and hatred among the three religious parties <note>Refers to the Catholics, Lutherans, and Reformed (Calvinists), the only three denominations legally recognized in the Holy Roman Empire.</note> that alone are lawful in Germany. It can be equally indifferent to me whether those intentions are true or unfounded, which other journalists and writers have already publicly

...accused me of. My complaint consists rather merely in the fact that those authors have dared, in their journal, to publicly and by name denounce me as a Jesuit of the fourth class <note>The "fourth class" refers to the highest rank of Jesuits who took a special vow of obedience to the Pope; in the 18th century, Protestant conspiracy theories often alleged that "secret Jesuits" had infiltrated Protestant institutions to undermine them from within.</note>. It could occur to no one less than to me that I, even I, was to be understood as one of the Protestant theologians described there as secret Jesuits of the fourth class. My theological principles lie before everyone's eyes in my writings: my treatise *On things carried over from Paganism into the Christian Religion* <note>original: "de Tralatitiis ex Gentilismo in Religionem christianam"</note>, my *Church History of the First Century*, my *Free-spirited Considerations on Christianity*, my *History of Arianism* <note>Arianism was an early Christian belief regarding the nature of Christ; Starck’s scholarly work on such topics was intended to prove his credentials as a rationalist Protestant academic.</note>, and others. Furthermore, I am not such an unknown man in Your Royal Majesty's states, since I have had the grace to stand in Your Highness's service for seven years and to hold the positions of Court Preacher, Chief Court Preacher, General Superintendent, and Professor of Theology at Königsberg—over whose faithful administration Your Royal Majesty expressed Your Highness's satisfaction to me in my dismissal decree. I also became a Doctor of Theology in Königsberg, and thus most solemnly bound myself to the maintenance of the Protestant system of doctrine.

It was therefore all the more unexpected to me when various friends reported to me that I was the one intended by these remarks. These hints, however, were not sufficient for me to undertake anything, and I therefore had to wait in patience for further developments and remain silent until I should be named. This has now happened in the July issue of the mentioned monthly journal, as they name me as the one of whom they claimed in the preceding issues that he was a Jesuit of the fourth class and also spoke of the priesthood in his sermons. They seek to give this black assertion a particular veneer by claiming that I belonged to the Knights Templar <note>A high-degree branch of Freemasonry that claimed descent from the medieval order; it was often accused of having secret Catholic or Jesuit influences.</note> among the Freemasons, and specifically to the so-called *Clerici* <note>The "Clerics" were a specific branch within the Rite of Strict Observance in Freemasonry, focused on spiritual and liturgical matters, of which Starck was a prominent founder.</note>, and they challenge me to defend myself against these accusations. To engage in disputes with unnamed authors who creep in the dark is neither appropriate for my office and rank, nor for my duties. In our Protestant Church, we also have no Court of Inquisition. Moreover, Your Royal Majesty will certainly not approve of some of Your subjects taking it upon themselves to establish such an inquisitorial tribunal—which, by declaring everything an attacked man might say in his writings as pretense, well-known Jesuit tricks, or even the effect of papal dispensations <note>A "dispensation" in this context refers to a perceived secret permission from the Pope allowing a Jesuit to lie or pose as a Protestant to further the Catholic cause.</note>, is far worse than the heretical chairs of the *Dominicans* in *Spain* and *Portugal*. Your Majesty will certainly not permit this self-appointed tribunal to cast suspicion upon the servants of other princes—who are Your Royal Majesty's fellow estates of the Empire—and to call them to account. In any case, publicly poured-out injuries cannot be the subject of a learned feud, but are suitable only for legal action, the pursuit of which rank, honor, good conscience, and self-preservation make my duty.

It is true, I was a Freemason in my younger years; it is true that when the so-called *Strict Observance* <note>The "Strict Observance" was a high-degree rite of Freemasonry popular in Germany, which claimed a secret succession from the medieval Knights Templar.</note> was introduced among the Freemasons, which sought to restore the Order of the Templars, I belonged to it, and just as others were *Knights*, *Associates*, *Squires*, *Commanders*, *Prefects*, and *Sub-Priors* <note>original: "Equites, Socii, Armigeri, Commendatores, Praefecti und Sub-Priores"</note>: indeed, some even took formal monastic vows, I was a *Cleric* <note>original: "Clericus"</note>, as many servants currently in Your Royal Majesty's states, all of whom can be named, belonged to it: but it never occurred to me or any other to spread Catholicism through it; rather, everything aimed to make the initiations and the then-so-called chapters more brilliant and more appropriate to the Order of Saint John <note>The Order of St. John (Johanniter) remained a prestigious Protestant chivalric order in Prussia, unlike the defunct Templars.</note>, which is surely not suspected of Catholicism and still exists in Your Royal Majesty's states. Far less have I ever been in indirect or direct connection with a Jesuit, and have in no way allowed myself to be used for the achievement of their real or alleged intentions, which I can, upon request before any lawful authority, testify to as fervently as can ever be demanded of me.

And these abominable accusations—which certainly did not flow from Christian love or Protestant zeal (for otherwise other paths would have been taken), but quite obviously with the intent to injure and harm <note>original: *animo injuriandi et nocendi*</note> me—are partly contained literally in the previously mentioned issues of the *Berlin Monthly Magazine* <note>The *Berliner Monatsschrift* was a leading journal of the German Enlightenment, which frequently attacked Starck for his perceived mystical and pro-Catholic tendencies.</note>, and partly flow from what is said there through the most natural conclusions.

For this, in the deepest humility, pleads:

to make tolerance suspect, as was claimed some time ago by **Weckhrlin** <note>Ludwig Ferdinand Huber Weckhrlin (1739–1792) was a controversial journalist and critic known for his provocative and often scandalous publications.</note>, or to introduce Naturalism <note>The belief that all events can be explained by natural causes, often used as a derogatory term for those who rejected divine revelation.</note>, as was accused of the Berliners by the Privy Councilor **Jacobi** <note>Friedrich Heinrich Jacobi (1743–1819), a philosopher who famously triggered the "Pantheism controversy" by accusing leading thinkers of atheistic tendencies.</note> and another unnamed author according to the *General Literary Journal*? This same man was challenged to defend himself against this, and—contrary to the legal principle: <note>original: "Affirmandi incumbit probatio"</note> *The burden of proof lies upon him who affirms*—he was tasked with proving that he was not one.

It could have occurred to no one less than myself that I was the one meant by this. Formerly, people had sought to brand me as a heretic for being a "new-thinking" theologian, indeed even a *Socinian* <note>A follower of Socinianism, a rationalist Christian movement that denied the Trinity; it was a common slur for those perceived as too "enlightened" or heterodox.</note>; and now I was supposed to belong to the other extreme, that I was a Jesuit and favored Catholicism in my sermons: the contradiction was too striking. My writings are in everyone's hands and testify most clearly to the contrary. I am a Doctor of Theology and have sworn an oath upon the symbolic books <note>The *Symbolic Books* are the official confessional documents of the Lutheran Church to which clergy must subscribe.</note>, and I cannot, therefore, be detrimental to our Protestant church without at the same time becoming a perjurer. Some of my sermons are in print and contain nothing that could awaken such a suspicion; and indeed, I compose and memorize them word-for-word, and can submit all the sermons I have ever held in my life—all of which I still possess—to any tribunal for the strictest revision. It was often unbelievable to me that I was the one intended. This was, however, reported to me by various friends, and among others by **Dr. Rosenmüller** in Leipzig and **Professor Schütz** in Jena. In the secure hope that men of weight would soon enough oppose this Naturalistic fanaticism—

As was done by **Prof. Garve** in Breslau <note>Christian Garve (1742–1798), a prominent philosopher of the German Enlightenment known for his translations of Cicero and Adam Smith.</note> and others regarding these matters, I thought it best to remain silent and not to stir until I was mentioned by name. I have never engaged in polemics; I hate all "wars of the pen," which are merely a waste of time and produce little good. Such conflicts are particularly ill-suited for me as an evangelical theologian, whose constant motto should be: **Love truth and peace!** <note>original: "Liebet Wahrheit und Frieden!" — a reference to Zechariah 8:19.</note> Furthermore, these were libels that qualified not for a scholarly debate, but for legal action. Finally, I was named in the *Berlin Monthly Magazine*, identified as the Protestant clergyman they had been discussing in previous issues. To confirm their claim, they cited that I formerly belonged to the **Knights Templar** <note>The "Strict Observance," a branch of Freemasonry that claimed descent from the medieval Knights Templar.</note> among the Freemasons—specifically to their **Clerics** <term>Clericis: the high-ranking "clerical" branch Starck founded, which focused on spiritual and liturgical secrets.</term>—and I was now called upon to defend myself against the accusations made against me.

I am duty-bound to give an account only to God and my lawful superiors, but not to private individuals who attempt to establish an **Inquisition tribunal** in the midst of Protestantism. They seek to disturb the peace of the Empire and of religion, casting suspicion on the servants of foreign princes who do not agree with their principles, or against whom they and their adherents may harbor private animosities and ulterior motives. Therefore, before my superiors, I confess that I became a Freemason in my younger years. I also confess that when a so-called "reform" was made among the Freemasons in the 1760s—which was intended to restore the defunct Order of the Temple—I joined it. Since the entire organization was to be modeled after the **Order of Saint John** <note>The Bailiwick of Brandenburg of the Chivalric Order of Saint John of the Hospital at Jerusalem, a Protestant order in Prussia.</note>—which still exists in the Prussian states and is certainly not suspected of Catholicism or Jesuitism—I belonged to the **Clerics** <note>original: "Clericis"</note> of this so-called Templar Order. I was joined by many others, including princes and distinguished men throughout Germany, among whom I will mention here only **Duke Ferdinand** and **Friedrich of Brunswick** <note>Ferdinand (1721–1792) and Friedrich August (1740–1805) of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel were high-ranking military leaders and prominent patrons of Freemasonry.</note>, who were **Knights**, **Squires**, **Associates** <note>original: "Equites, Armigeri, Socii"</note>, and so on. But it occurred to no one to favor Catholicism in this way, and even less was there the slightest hint of "Jesuitism" involved. In my entire life, I have never had the most distant indirect or direct connection with a Jesuit; indeed, I have never even spoken to one, which I can solemnly swear—

## D.

### High-born Sir!
### Most Highly Revered Secret Minister of State, War,
### and the Cabinet!

To Your High-born Excellency, at the end of July, I took the most obedient liberty of presenting my bill of complaint directed against the authors and publishers of the *Berlin Monthly Magazine* <note>Berlinische Monatsschrift: the primary journal of the Berlin Enlightenment, which frequently attacked Starck for his perceived religious conservatism and suspected secret ties to the Catholic Church.</note>. Hitherto, I have looked forward in vain to the just outcome of my righteous complaint. In the philanthropic character of Your High-born Excellency, I have all the just confidence that You would have already acceded to my most obedient request, had Your Excellency not been overwhelmed with too many important affairs due to the death of the most blessed Monarch <note>King Frederick the Great of Prussia, who died on August 17, 1786. Starck is acknowledging that the transition of power to Frederick William II has delayed administrative responses.</note>. Since my honor and my peace have been most sensitively wounded by the slanders spread against me by the writers of the *Berlin Monthly*, Your Excellency will forgive me—to whom nothing is dearer than his honor—that I herewith most obediently bring my concern to Your remembrance once again.

## F.

->Most Serene, Most Mighty King,<-
->Most Gracious King and Lord!<-

It is known to the whole world what has been said since the beginning of last year in the *Berlin Monthly Magazine*, edited by Doctor Biester and Senior Consistory Councilor Gedike, regarding the secret machinations of the Catholics and Jesuits to the detriment of Protestantism. I shall leave it undecided whether those secret efforts are well-founded, and if they were well-founded, whether they could ever be carried out; whether the violence of expression with which they are written about in said monthly magazine can coexist with the rational tolerance which owes its first existence to the Christian, enlightened principles of the most praiseworthy Prussian government, and which now seems to be spreading beneficially throughout all of Germany; and whether through that violence, mistrust, suspicion, and hatred are being rekindled anew between the three religious parties <note>A reference to the three denominations legally recognized in the Holy Roman Empire since the Peace of Westphalia: Roman Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed (Calvinist).</note> alone recognized by law in Germany. It can be equally matters of indifference to me whether those intentions are true or unfounded which other journalists and writers have already publicly accused the editors of the monthly magazine of harboring. Rather, my complaint consists solely in the fact that those editors have presumed to publicly decry me by name in their journal as a "Jesuit of the fourth class." <note>The "fourth class" refers to the highest rank of the Jesuit Order, those who have taken a special fourth vow of obedience to the Pope. To call a prominent Protestant theologian a "Jesuit of the fourth class" was an accusation of being a secret, high-level agent of the Catholic Church.</note>

# Supplements to the First Part,

In January, April, August, and December 1785, and in January, February, etc., 1786, it was stated in the aforementioned monthly magazine that a certain Protestant theologian was participating in these secret machinations, was a **Jesuit of the 4th Class**, <note>The "fourth vow" of the Jesuits is one of absolute obedience to the Pope regarding missions. In the 18th century, conspiracy theorists used the term "Jesuit of the 4th Class" to describe alleged secret agents who remained outwardly Protestant to subvert the church from within.</note> and was allowing [Catholic] ideas of the priesthood to influence his sermons. It could not have occurred to anyone less than myself that I—even I—was to be understood as the Protestant theologian depicted there as a secret Jesuit of the 4th Class. My theological principles are evident to everyone’s eyes in my writings: my *Treatise on the Transfers from Paganism into the Christian Religion*, <note>original: "Abhandlung de Tralatitiis ex Gentilismo in Religionem Christianam"</note> my *Church History of the First Century*, my *Frank Reflections on Christianity*, my *History of Arianism*, and others. Furthermore, I am not a man so unknown in Your Royal Majesty's states, having had the grace to hold the positions of Court Preacher, Chief Court Preacher, General Superintendent, and Professor of Theology at Königsberg. Regarding my faithful administration of these offices, the late King's Majesty <note>Frederick the Great (reigned 1740–1786).</note> expressed His Highest satisfaction to me in my decree of dismissal. I also became a Doctor of Theology in Königsberg and have thus most solemnly pledged myself to the maintenance of the Protestant system of doctrine. It was, therefore, all the more unexpected to me when various friends reported that I was the one intended. These hints, however, were not sufficient for me to take action, and I therefore had to wait in patience for further developments and remain silent until I should be named. This has now occurred in the July issue of the mentioned monthly magazine, where I am named as the one whom they claimed in previous installments was a Jesuit of the 4th Class and who speaks of the priesthood in his sermons. They seek to give this dark allegation a special veneer of truth by claiming that among the Freemasons I belong to the Templars, specifically to the so-called **Clerici**, <note>A branch of the "Strict Observance" Freemasons who claimed spiritual descent from the medieval Knights Templar; Starck was a high-ranking member of this group.</note> and they challenge me to defend myself against these accusations. With the approval of all laws, I hold to the principle that those who spread injuries <note>original: "Injurien"; here meaning legal libels or slanders.</note> against me—whether they devised them themselves or received them from others—act wrongly. It is enough that they truly spread these across the whole world without hesitation, even boasting and taking pride in performing such "neat work." In our Protestant Church, we have no court of Inquisition, and Your Royal Majesty will surely not approve of certain subjects taking it upon themselves to establish such an Inquisitional tribunal. Such a body, by declaring in advance that everything an attacked man might say in his writings is mere dissimulation, well-known Jesuit tricks <note>original: "Jesuitenkniffe." A common anti-Catholic trope suggesting that Jesuits used clever mental gymnastics or lies to hide their true intentions.</note>, or even the effect of papal dispensations <note>Special permissions from the Pope to bypass church laws, often used here to suggest that a secret Catholic could lie under oath or live as a Protestant without sinning.</note>, thereby cuts off every other form of defense. Consequently, it is far worse than the heresy-seats of the Dominicans in Spain and Portugal. Your Majesty will certainly not allow this self-appointed tribunal to cast suspicion upon and demand accountability from the ministers of other princes who are Your Royal Majesty's fellow Estates of the Empire. In any case, publicly poured-out injuries cannot be the subject of a learned feud; rather, they are suitable only for legal action, the pursuit of which is made my duty by my rank, honor, good conscience, and self-preservation.

It is true, I was a Freemason in my younger years; it is also true that when the so-called Strict Observance <note>A branch of Freemasonry that claimed a direct historical descent from the medieval Knights Templar. It was known for its hierarchical structure and focus on chivalric and occult themes.</note> was introduced among the Freemasons—that is, when it was quite generally believed among Masons in and out of Germany that the true secret of the Order consisted in the secret, quiet continuation of the Order of the Templars—I belonged to it. The main idea, therefore, was to restore the Order of the Templars. If members wished to enter the so-called high or inner orders, they first had to endure a certain novitiate; then they became **Knights**, **Associates**, **Arms-bearers**, **Commanders**, **Prefects**, **Sub-Priors**, and **Priors** <note>original: "Equites, Socii, Armigeri, Commendatores, Praefecti, Sub-Priores und Priores"</note>. Indeed, there were even a notable number of them who made a formal monastic profession "according to the rule of St. Bernard of Clairvaux" <note>original: "Secundum regulam St. Bernardi, Clarevallenſis"</note> and vowed monastic obedience (**Professed Knights** <note>original: "Equites professi"</note>). Others, including myself—as well as many servants located within Your Royal Majesty’s states, all of whom are well-known...

simply because I belonged **among the Clerics** <note>original: "inter Clericos." Yet, if one wants to engage in word-splitting and letter-hunting, those expressions like **Associates**, **Priors**, **Sub-Priors**, **Professed members**, and the vowed **Obedience** <term>Obedience: In this context, a formal vow of submission to a superior, a practice typical of monastic and chivalric orders.</term> smack far more of Catholicism—and specifically Jesuitism—than the innocent name of a **Cleric**, which is a title suitable for all Christian religions. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;I could least of all have imagined that letters written in a fit of **enthusiasm**, which clearly show they were produced by a desire to research the secrets of the Order, could be held against me. Men of greater intellect, insight, and experience let themselves be carried away by that same enthusiasm, and this desire had become the fashionable obsession of the time. Or how can it be framed as a dangerous undertaking when a man, who had the opportunity to learn the conduct and **cipher-language** <note>original: "Chiffre-Sprache." Coded communication used by secret societies to hide their messages from outsiders.</note> of the many secret societies then in vogue, seeks to investigate a newly emerging **secret-monger** <note>original: "Geheimniß-Krämer." A person who makes a trade of mystery or pretends to possess hidden knowledge.</note> using that same cipher-language? Is it not too hasty and unkind to make him an ally of all **fanatics** <note>original: "Schwärmer." A derogatory term used in the 18th century for religious visionaries, mystics, or those perceived as irrationally enthusiastic.</note> and to willfully ignore the obvious intention of investigating such fanatics? # Supplement to the first part.

That attempted union of those Freemasons who had adopted the **Templar system** partly in the form of **knights** and partly as **clerics** <note>original: "Clerici." These were the two main branches of the "Strict Observance" rite of Freemasonry.</note> eventually made such an impression on me that—as was already happening then and even more so later among the most insightful Masons—I gradually learned to see the emptiness, instability, unsustainability, and uncertainty of the entire system and the **Strict Observance** <term>Strict Observance: A Masonic rite that claimed a direct descent from the medieval Knights Templar and demanded absolute obedience to hidden leaders.</term> grafted onto it. I ceased to involve myself further with the **Knights**, *Socii* <note>original: "Sociis," meaning associates or companions.</note>, **Esquires**, **Priors**, and **Bernardine Professed** <note>These were specific hierarchical ranks within the Templar-inspired Masonic system.</note>. I also withdrew from any idea of a **Templar Clericate** and finally—having been made wise enough through various vexations and adverse fates over more than nine years—I turned away from everything that is and is called Freemasonry so quietly that I no longer take even the most remote part in it.

Despite this, and although the Templar system and the Strict Observance were subsequently said to have been formally abolished by the Masons themselves at the **Convent of Wilhelmsbad** <note>A famous Masonic congress held in 1782 where the "Strict Observance" was reorganized and its claims of Templar descent were largely abandoned.</note>, and despite such things being specifically forbidden in Your Royal Majesty's lands, I am nevertheless the only one who, after such a long passage of time, is dragged back into the spotlight by the hair, as it were. I alone am the one people seek to insult and brand a heretic; they seek to rob me of my honor and good name, and perhaps even my bread and my service, through a cabal that hostile people must necessarily have spun, and through an injury that is the most abominable of its kind.

For when one publicly trumpets a *Doctor of Theology* <note>original: "Doctorem Theologiæ."</note>—who solemnly pledged himself at his promotion to the maintenance of the **Protestant doctrine**, and who is at the same time the **Senior Court Chaplain** <note>original: "Oberhofprediger," the highest-ranking ecclesiastical position in a princely court.</note> and first clergyman of a distinguished Protestant principality, as well as the confessor of one of the most distinguished German Protestant princely houses so closely related to the Royal House—through a publicly printed monthly journal throughout all of Germany, not only as a **secret Catholic** but even as a member of an order suppressed by **papal bulls** and rejected as dangerous throughout all of Catholic Christendom, and especially as one of its most dangerous members (namely of the **Fourth Class** <note>This likely refers to the "Professed of the Fourth Vow" in the Jesuit Order, the highest and most secretive rank, which fueled many conspiracy theories of the era.</note>), and shouts this with such assumed audacity that one even summons him for examination and testing before an arbitrarily established literary *forum* <note>original: "Forum," referring to a court or tribunal of public opinion.</note>—

...claims, and blames him for the spread of **Catholicism** in his sermons: this constitutes the darkest **injury** <note>original: "Injurie." In this context, it refers to a legal and moral libel or slander against one's reputation.</note> against such a man, which most grossly violates his honor and good name. It makes him out to be a perjurer and a most dangerous **falsifier** <note>original: "Falsarius," a Latin term for a forger or someone who acts under false pretenses.</note> who intends nothing less than to disturb the peace and contentment of the **Princely family** through secret conversions, or otherwise to carry out **Jesuitical tricks** <note>In the 18th century, "Jesuitical tricks" was a common pejorative for perceived Catholic subversion and intellectual dishonesty.</note> in some other way. This is an injury that puts him in danger of experiencing highly unpleasant decrees from his superiors, which could rob him of the confidence of his sovereign and the Princely family, make him suspicious to his fellow citizens, and even deprive him of his bread and service. For even if one wishes to think—and by the laws of the **Empire** <note>This refers to the Peace of Westphalia, which legally recognized three denominations in the Holy Roman Empire: Roman Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed (Calvinist).</note> must think—ever so tolerantly of the transition from one of the three legal churches in Germany to another; nevertheless, the person who, while holding honor, reputation, and bread from the one church to which he publicly professes, is nonetheless secretly devoted to the other church, and should even wish to make **proselytes** <term>Proselytes: New converts, often implying those won over through aggressive or secret persuasion.</term> in a Princely house, is the most consummate villain and the most depraved human being upon whom the sun shines.

And these abominable accusations—certainly poured out against me not from Christian love or Protestant zeal (for otherwise other paths would have been taken), but quite obviously **with the intention of injuring and harming** <note>original: "animo iniuriandi et nocendi."</note>—are partly contained verbatim in the previously mentioned issues of the ***Berlin Monthly*** <note>original: "Berliner Monatsschrift," a leading journal of the German Enlightenment (Aufklärung).</note>, and partly flow from what was said there through the most natural conclusions. Long before anyone knew anything of the book ***Anti-Nicaise*** <note>One of Starck's major works defending himself against accusations of secret Catholicism.</note>, the editors of the *Berlin Monthly* saw fit to have the following placed in the issue of January 1785, page 62, through an alleged extract of a letter from * * *:

> I myself have visited a Protestant theologian, well-known through his writings, of whom it is already almost publicly said that he is not only **affiliated with the Jesuits**, but is himself a **Jesuit of the Fourth Class** <note>The "Fourth Vow" is the highest level of Jesuit initiation, involving special obedience to the Pope regarding missions; being accused of this was a claim that one was a top-tier secret agent.</note>, from the class which must take the vow to allow themselves to be used for missions. This will seem incredible to the majority of Protestants. But these things are nevertheless true, **reliably true**.

### Supplements to the First Part.

In any case, the editors of the **Monthly** <note>original: "Monatsschrift," referring to the *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, a leading journal of the German Enlightenment.</note> had already taken precautions to be able to retreat behind the cover of an anonymous author; yet in April of that same year, on page 345, they carefully extended this caution further, stating that the author, the person who sent the piece, and the editors of that article were three completely different people. But even this safety was not yet great enough, for in August 1785, on page 106, there appeared no fewer than four different parties: the author, the sender, the correspondent, and the editors. In the same article, on page 149, they hedge in another way, saying they did not claim that the **Protestant theologian** <note>Starck refers to himself in the third person here, as the journals did when attacking him.</note> was a **Jesuit**, but only that it was being said almost publicly that he was—though anyone who reads the first claim extracted above can understand nothing else but this:

> That the Protestant theologian is a Jesuit,
> that it is true, and so reliably true, that it
> is already being said almost publicly.

Who does not recognize from this the malice of my enemies? First, they want to bring a **rumor** <note>original: "bruit," a French term for noise or public report commonly used in 18th-century German prose.</note> into the world through the *Monthly* that there is a Protestant clergyman in the Rhine region who is a secret Jesuit. Afterward, through secret **insinuations**, they likely ensured that I would be the one named among the people (for before the attack in the *Monthly*, no one had even thought of it). Finally, however, after they achieved their aim—having done so much themselves that it was being spoken of almost publicly—they cleverly retreated behind various anonymous informants and the ambiguity of their report.

Meanwhile, in this very same article, two "facts" are stated on page 151:
1) That the Protestant theologian had a **tonsure** <note>The shaving of the crown of the head, a practice for Catholic monks and priests. For a Protestant preacher to have one would be "proof" of a secret conversion.</note>,
2) that his sermons sounded completely different from the sermons of a Protestant, and that he often affected talk of the **priesthood** <note>original: "Priesterthum." In a Protestant context, this was often viewed with suspicion as "popish" or "sacerdotalist."</note>.

Where is the person who has ever seen a tonsure on me? Let him stand up and say it aloud. The reproach that my sermons do not sound Protestant is more than shameless, since they have not produced even a single circumstance as proof—

Nevertheless, in the Protestant Church, in theological compendiums, Christians are presented as learned priests; indeed, children in schools are already taught the Threefold Office of Christ the Lord, namely the **Royal**, the **High Priestly**, and the **Prophetic** office. This is what justice, fairness, and the innocence of an honest man demand—a man who, for reasons incomprehensible to him, is so maliciously hated, so bitterly persecuted, and who is to be thrust into misery and contempt if possible.

Now, even if the editors of the *Berlin Monthly* should excuse themselves by saying that the essays concerning me were not their own work but were sent in by others, they have nevertheless—as I have proven above—presented themselves *of their own accord* <note>original: "proprio motu"</note> as busy, active <term>propagators</term> <note>original: "Propalatores." From the Latin, meaning those who publicize or spread information, especially libelous content.</note> of the insults poured out against me in the following issues of the journal. Even if they were not to be held accountable at least as <term>editors</term> <note>original: "editores"</note> of the injurious pieces, they are still bound by all laws to name the authors, submitters, and correspondents exactly to me, so that I can seek redress from them. This is necessary so that the *Monthly* itself, in the absence of this founded <term>legal remedy</term> <note>original: "Rechtshülfe"</note>, does not degenerate from an otherwise useful journal into a public <term>collection of pasquinades</term> <note>original: "Pasquillen-Sammlung." A pasquinade is a public satire or lampoon, often anonymous and libelous, posted in a public place.</note>, in which every anonymous person can embolden himself to cut off the honor and good name of his innocent fellow man undetected and unpunished, while the innocent man remains robbed of all legal recourse. 

Therefore, I most submissively and humbly implore Your Royal Majesty to allow justice to be done to me, so that the editors of those pieces in the *Berlin Monthly* be most justly compelled, *under a fixed deadline* <note>original: "sub termino praefigendo"</note>, to provide judicial proof of the highly defamatory accusations they have publicly leveled against me and deliberately spread—especially that I am a <term>Jesuit priest of the fourth class</term> <note>In anti-Jesuit conspiracy theories of the time, "fourth class" Jesuits were whispered to be secret agents who had taken a special vow of obedience and could pass as Protestants to subvert the church from within.</note>, and that I also seek to spread <term>Catholicism</term> <note>original: "Katholicismus"</note> through my sermons. In the event of their failure to provide proof, they should be held to the most striking public and private <term>satisfaction</term> <note>original: "Genugthuung." A legal term for formal redress or an apology meant to restore a person's honor.</note>. At the very least, if they excuse themselves by claiming that all the essays and remarks in the *Monthly* were written and sent by others, and if this excuse should legally take effect, they should then be compelled to name the authors, submitters, and correspondents, by means of taking a physical oath <note>original: "körperlichen Eides"</note> that they will not conceal anyone.

Therefore, and because in the absence of acquaintance, a conscientious [man], standing in no connection with my opponents...

# G.

->Most humble and obedient report.<-

I find myself obliged to a High Princely and most Honorable Ministry, in accordance with my previous humble report of July 26, 1786, to further and most obediently report that I had sent my complaint to the Royal Minister, <term>Count von Herzberg</term> <note>Ewald Friedrich, Count von Herzberg (1725–1795), was a powerful Prussian statesman who served as a minister of state and played a key role in Prussian foreign policy.</note>. This was due to my lack of acquaintance and ignorance regarding the legal procedures in Berlin, as well as the doubts I had regarding the proper <term>forum</term> <note>original: "Forum." In a legal context, this refers to the specific court or jurisdiction that has the authority to hear a case.</note> of the defendants. A few days ago, I received his reply, stating that he had called the Berlin journalists to account. Since they have now excused themselves by claiming that the essays directed against me did not originate from them—and therefore believed they deserved some leniency—it remains open to me either to be satisfied with this or to file the complaint at the <term>Kammergericht</term> <note>The highest court of justice in Berlin, which handled significant civil and criminal matters.</note> in Berlin, as the defendants' proper jurisdiction, and to authorize a Justice Commissioner there. Since I cannot and will not be satisfied with that meager excuse, and now that I finally know the defendants' pretexts and can proceed more directly with the matter; I have today actually sent the somewhat modified and expanded complaint directly to the High Court in Berlin. I therefore most devotedly attach a faithful copy of it, refer otherwise to my previous report, commend myself to the just protection of a High Ministry, and wait in devout respect
->Of a High Princely and most Honorable Ministry<-
Darmstadt, the 27th of
October 1786.
Humble
D. Starck.

### H.

->High-born Lord Count,<-
->Highly Honored Lord Privy State, War,<-
->and Cabinet Minister,<-
->Gracious Lord!<-

I humbly thank Your High-Countly Excellency for the gracious letter of the 7th of this month. Just as I saw with true peace of mind that you deigned to give my just complaint such consideration as to preliminarily hear the defense of the editors of the <term>Berlin Monthly</term> <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, a leading journal of the German Enlightenment, often critical of religious orthodoxy.</note>, I also consider it my duty to report in humble respect that those editors have nevertheless diligently endeavored to further spread the accusations brought into the *Monthly* under their own names in various further pieces, even before the slightest mention was made of me in any other printed book. They also mainly think to excuse themselves with the claim that the essays were sent to them by other authors <term>for publication</term> <note>original: "ad publicandum." A Latin legal and publishing term.</note>. 

Since I then know of no other way to defend and save my so grossly attacked honor and good name, given the situation, than by legal means, I have actually sent the somewhat more extended complaint to the Royal <term>Kammergericht</term> <note>The highest court of appeal in the Prussian judicial system.</note> according to Your High-Countly Excellency's gracious instruction. I have attached the <term>petitum</term> <note>original: "petitum." The formal request or specific relief sought by a plaintiff in a lawsuit.</note> to at least compel the editors to name the authors, submitters, and correspondents of all pieces concerning me from the previous and current year by means of a <term>bodily oath</term> <note>original: "körperlichen Eides." A solemn oath, often involving physical contact with a sacred object, used to ensure the truth of a statement in court.</note>. This is so that I am put in a position to further pursue my rights and am not left in an <term>unequal match</term> <note>original: "partie inegale." A French term for an unfair contest where one party is at a disadvantage.</note>, fighting against my bitter enemies who are hidden behind the cover of the *Berlin Monthly*.

In this regard, I must not conceal from Your High-Countly Excellency that I have most humbly recommended the justice of my cause to His Royal Majesty—to whom I have the invaluable luck of being personally known—on October 8th, thus earlier than I had the luck of receiving your gracious reply. From his love of justice...

<meta>This page continues Johann August Starck’s formal legal response and narrative regarding his lawsuit against the editors of the Berlin Monthly. Having just appointed his lawyer, Michaelis, Starck now outlines the specific defamatory claims made against him that form the basis of his case.</meta>

In order to comply with the highest command <note>Refers to the instruction from the Prussian King mentioned on the previous page.</note> with the most devoted readiness, I wish to present the main points even more clearly, if possible, for the sake of greater evidence.

The editors of the *Berlin Monthly* <note>The *Berlinische Monatsschrift*, the influential journal of the Berlin Enlightenment led by Gedike and Biester.</note> began by printing in their journal: that a certain Protestant clergyman of the first rank was a secret Jesuit. They continued by announcing that this Protestant theologian was a cleric, a Jesuit priest, possessed the tonsure <note>The practice of shaving the hair from the scalp as a sign of religious devotion or admission to an order; a clear accusation that the Protestant Starck had secretly converted to Catholicism.</note>, and was, in short, a "Jesuit of the fourth class." <note>The "fourth class" or "Professed of the Four Vows" represents the highest tier of the Jesuit Order, who take a special vow of obedience to the Pope regarding missions.</note> Not content with merely asserting that the man was "afflicted" with Jesuitism, they further sought to prove that he was not among the "deceived" <note>Meaning he wasn't a pawn, but a conscious conspirator.</note>, but rather that he applied himself actively to the practice of Jesuitism. For they said of him: he well knows what he is doing, he delivers Jesuitical sermons, and in them affects to speak of the priesthood. Were Mr. Gedike and Mr. Biester themselves present in the Princely Court Church in Darmstadt to hear these sermons?

Thus, the Protestant theologian was not only a Jesuit of the fourth class, but was also active as such, seeking through his teachings to spread Jesuitism among both his high-ranking and common listeners. And this was blamed upon him long before the masked author of the *Anti-Nicaise* <note>A polemical work by Friedrich Nicolai attacking Starck; "Nicaise" refers to a character in a story by Jean de La Fontaine, used here to mock Starck's supposed mystical-Catholic tendencies.</note> saw fit to come forward against me. The journalists did not yet name me publicly, but it must have happened all the more diligently in secret, as friends informed me that I was the one intended.

As soon as the anonymous author of the second part of the *Anti-St. Nicaise* saw fit to attack me publicly, I was then also taken up in the *Berlin Monthly*, whereby its authors or editors added more of their own, assuring readers that everything previously asserted in that journal regarding the "Protestant theologian" had applied to me. They thus still maintain that I am not only the Jesuit priest of the fourth class, but also that I am not among the deceived, that I hold Jesuitical sermons, and affect to speak of the priesthood in them—which latter claims (unless they were taken from the *Monthly* itself) never even occurred to the author of the *Anti-St. Nicaise*, but are the original inventions of the Berlin journalists.

### Supplements to the First Part.

Since I have already presented all of this in my lawsuit, I must maintain that a clear, complete, and coherent narrative of the <term>facts of the case</term> <note>original Latin: *Facti*.</note>—upon which I, the plaintiff, base my legal claim—could very easily be drafted from my lawsuit by whoever is responsible for reporting on it. The evidence for everything lies printed before one's eyes in the issues of the *Berlin Monthly* cited in my claim. That a just cause for legal action belongs to me based on these facts is something that surely no person can doubt. I have set forth in my lawsuit that it is the most shameful, dangerous, and detestable <term>fraud</term> <note>original Latin: *Falsum*. In this legal context, it refers to a criminal deception or a fundamental misrepresentation of identity.</note> when a Protestant <term>Doctor of Theology</term> <note>original Latin: *Doctor Theologiae*.</note> and <term>Senior Court Preacher</term> <note>German: *Oberhofprediger*; a high-ranking clergyman serving a princely family, in this case, the Landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt.</note> to a Princely family is simultaneously an actively functioning secret Jesuit. I have argued that such a man, who has forgotten his duty and committed perjury, deserves to lose his honor, his office, and his bread. Who could possibly deny an innocent man the right to sue when another dares to accuse him, both secretly and publicly, of this most loathsome fraud? This is especially true when the poisonous <term>cabal</term> <note>German: *Kabale*; a group of people united in a secret plot or intrigue.</note> has arranged the matter so artfully and cunningly that they wish to force the innocent man to undertake, as it were, the <term>proof of a negative</term> <note>original Latin: *probationem negativae*. In law, proving that something did *not* happen—such as proving one is *not* a secret Jesuit—is considered a nearly impossible burden of proof.</note>. This is particularly difficult when every step the insulted party might take in public to rescue his innocence is already declared in advance to be spiteful disguise, the result of a <term>papal dispensation</term> <note>A formal exemption from church law. Starck’s enemies suggested the Pope had given him secret permission to pretend to be a Protestant.</note>, and so forth. If no rescue is to be found here in the courts, then innocence suffers and the evil persecutor achieves his aim.

I am well aware that the <term>journalists</term> <note>Referring specifically to Friedrich Gedike and Johann Erich Biester, the editors of the *Berlin Monthly*.</note> will likely intend to excuse themselves in the usual manner: by claiming that the main charges against me were in a printed book, that they were sent to them by correspondents, or even that they were anonymous essays. However, I have already proven in my lawsuit that the journalists spoke in their own persons from time to time. I have further proven that they wrote against me partly before anyone had even thought of the *Anti-St. Nicaise* <note>A famous anonymous polemic of the time that accused Starck of crypto-Catholicism.</note>, and partly that they put forward things of which not a single word appears in the *Anti-St. Nicaise*. And how can a literary weekly, which is printed under the Highest Royal Approval and is intended to serve the spread of the sciences and useful literary knowledge, be so abused that honest people are branded within it, and—

<meta>This page continues Johann August Starck’s legal complaint against the editors of the Berlin Monthly. He is arguing that the accusations of him being a secret Jesuit are baseless and that the editors should be held legally responsible for the anonymous content they publish.</meta>

<page-num>608</page-num>

### Supplements to the First Part.

...that such a thing is raised to a more than Jesuitical heresy trial, in which people presume to hold an **auto-da-fé** <note>original: *Auto da Fe*; Portuguese for "act of faith," referring to the public sentencing and execution of heretics during the Inquisition.</note> over the most blameless men at their whim; and for what reasons? Based on mere conjectures, ambiguous interpretations, word-picking, and things that happened 20 years ago and were long forgotten—things which, if they deserved a reprimand, should not be visited upon one man pulled from the crowd, but upon many thousands who were in the same **Masonic** <note>original: *maurerischer*; referring to Freemasonry, which was often viewed with suspicion or linked to secret religious agendas during this period.</note> society, and who in part held far more striking titles, such as Princes, Counts, Generals, Ministers of State, etc.

If, according to all laws, the editor of a **journal** must answer for everything and anything that appears in his **journal**, whether he wrote it himself or it was sent to him: then I have a just claim against the editors of the *Berlin Monthly*, and they may **seek recourse** <note>original: *regressiren*; a legal term meaning to seek indemnification or turn to their own sources to cover the liability.</note> against their accomplices. I can therefore, with every right, seek the salvation of my so shamefully tarnished honor against them and demand just satisfaction—all the more so as they are, until now, the only ones known to me among the secret **injurers** <note>original: *Injurianten*; those who have committed a legal injury or libel.</note>. Against whom else should I **prosecute** <note>original: *prosequiren*; to pursue or continue a legal action.</note> my just complaint, since no one else has identified themselves?

At the very least, they are bound to identify their correspondents under oath, and also to publish the anonymous essays with all the knowledge they have of them under oath.

I believe I have now said enough. Should there perhaps still be something to supplement here and there according to the **court style** <note>original: *stilo curiae*; the formal procedural and linguistic requirements of the specific court.</note used there, I only ask for news and instruction. A foreigner, who moreover is not **of the trade** <note>meaning he is a theologian/clergyman, not a professional lawyer.</note>, will certainly deserve such indulgence. I have a completely firm and certain confidence that a Highly Esteemed Royal **Chamber Court** <note>original: *Kammergericht*; the highest court of justice in Prussia, based in Berlin.</note> will grant me just help against the defamers of my honor and my bitter persecutors. I request Your Well-Born to take up the cause of such grossly slandered innocence with dutiful warmth, and in this trustful anticipation, I have the honor to be with all respect,

->Your Well-Born<-

Darmstadt,
Nov. 27, 1786.
->obedient servant<-
->*Starck*<-

<summary>Johann August Starck concludes his formal complaint against the editors of the Berlin Monthly, demanding they be held accountable for libel and identifying them as his only known legal targets. He appeals to the Royal Chamber Court in Berlin for justice, styling himself as an innocent foreigner unfamiliar with Prussian legal technicalities.</summary>
